characters.name: Carmela Soprano
characters.description: Tony Soprano's often conflicted wife. She enjoys the lifestyle that Tony's money brings her, but struggles to cope with his infidelity and the dirtier aspects to his profession. As a result, there's no shortage of conflict between the two over the course of the series. Actually Pretty Funny: When Janice says that Richie's time in prison has given him a deeper sensitivity to the plight of women, Carmela can't help but laugh at the absurdity of the statement. Affectionate Nickname: "Carm". Her father sometimes calls her "Mel" or "Mellie". All for Nothing: She desperately wants her daughter Meadow to be able to escape the Mafia life, and goes out of her way to shield the latter from its excesses. But she keeps hammering into Meadow that the government persecutes "Italians" (i.e. Mafiosos) until she makes her believe it, and Meadow eventually decides to become a lawyer who defends mobsters. All Girls Want Bad Boys: States on multiple occasions that Tony being a gangster makes their courtship more exciting,in spite of all the problems it brings her personally. Later on, she lusts after Furio, one of Tony's most ruthless (yet by far the most cultured, sensitive, and fit) enforcers.

characters.name: Meadow Soprano
characters.description: Tony and Carmela's daughter and oldest child. Smart, ambitious, and hardworking, she spends much of the series grappling with the implications of her family's lifestyle. Amoral Attorney: The finale implies she's on her way to becoming one as she starts to favor law over a medical degree. Armor-Piercing Question:She delivers one to AJ, who at that point was still ignorant of what Tony does for a living.Do you know any other garbagemen who live in a house like this?Meadow to her dad in an early season one episode: "Are you in the mafia?" She delivers one to AJ, who at that point was still ignorant of what Tony does for a living. Meadow to her dad in an early season one episode: "Are you in the mafia?"

characters.name: Anthony "AJ" Soprano Jr.
characters.description: Tony and Carmela's son and youngest child. He's a spoiled kid with little direction in life, who struggles to find purpose and meaning for himself. Acrofatic: Despite being overweight in his early teenage years, he's good at sports. He places third at a swim meet after narrowly missing out on second place and later joins the high school football team, where he becomes a defensive captain after starting off as a bench player. Ancestral Name: Named after his father, Anthony. Beard of Sorrow: Grows one during hisbreakup with Blanca and suicide attempt. Be Careful What You Wish For: Moves in with his father for a while when his parents are separated because Carmela disciplines him, but it doesn't work as Tony is not a fun pushover.

characters.name: Corrado "Junior" Soprano
characters.description: Tony's uncle andde jureboss of the Soprano crime family. Affably Evil: Junior is generally a genial and friendly old man with a wicked sense of humor, so long as you don't get in his way. Alas, Poor Villain:His last appearance in Season 6's episode "Made in America". It is clear that his Alzheimer's has progressed to the point he is unaware of his surroundings and remembers nothing of his past other than playing catch with Tony. Seeing what his uncle has become almost reduces Tony to tears. All for Nothing:Much of his time in the series is spent trying to avoid being convicted and sent to prison for racketeering charges. He eventually succeeds after several years of house arrest, but he soon develops dementia and is permanently confined to a mental institution after mistaking Tony for a long-dead enemy and shooting him, rendering the entire endeavour pointless.Most of the first season is a broiling conflict between Tony and Junior over leadership of the crime family. It's ultimately made a moot point by the end of the season due to aDeus ex Machina, where the FBI indicts Junior on charges that been completely unmentioned until that point, taking him out of the conflict without Tony having to do anything. It gets even worse whenhe develops dementia and it worsens to the point he can't even remember he was ever a mobster or who Tony even is. Much of his time in the series is spent trying to avoid being convicted and sent to prison for racketeering charges. He eventually succeeds after several years of house arrest, but he soon develops dementia and is permanently confined to a mental institution after mistaking Tony for a long-dead enemy and shooting him, rendering the entire endeavour pointless.

characters.name: Livia Soprano
characters.description: Tony's hateful and abusive mother. She's a spiteful, selfish, narcissistic woman who only seems to take joy in making others miserable. Abusive Parents: A real piece of work who threatened to stick a fork in Tony's eye when he was 10 years old, among many other examples. When Dr. Melfi asks Tony if he can recall any 'warm, loving memories' of her from his childhood, Tony is genuinely trying hard to come up with any specific ones for a full minute and the only one he can think of is when his father hurt himself in front of everyone. Accentuate the Negative: Livia's favorite pastime. She never has a good word to say about anything or anyone. Or, as put by her own granddaughter:Janice:You know Grandma pretty well, don't you?Meadow:I guess...Janice:What is she into?Meadow:*smiling wryly* I dunno...Negativity?A discussion where Tony brings up Dr. Melfi's theories with Janice mentions that Livia is incapable of happiness. A discussion where Tony brings up Dr. Melfi's theories with Janice mentions that Livia is incapable of happiness. Alas, Poor Villain:Downplayedwith her death inProshai, Livushka. While an abusive monster par excellence and all-aroundJerkass, Livia's death is treated in a somewhat somber manner, as it's clear that she drove everyone who could have loved her away and dies all alone, not even wanting a funeral, aslampshadedby Carmela. As horrible as Livia was, her death does have some pathos, even if theharm she inflictedand contempt she (deservedly)earned from othersis emphasized first and foremost.In Camelotgives a far more straightforward example when she suffered a near-fatal miscarriage only to beignored by Johnny as he cheated on her. Seeing Livia in such a sorry state while being abandoned and lied to by her own husband casts her in a very different light than just a one-note abusiveHate Sink.

characters.name: Janice Soprano
characters.description: Older sister of Tony Soprano who lives in Seattle at the start of the series. Abusive Parents:Much like Tony, she was the victim of this in the form of her spiteful mother, Livia, who relentlessly criticized her appearance as well as her failed string of romantic relationships.She later becomes a pretty bad parent to Bobby Baccala’s kids, as they see through her charades easily, and after his death, the kids are stuck with her alone. Much like Tony, she was the victim of this in the form of her spiteful mother, Livia, who relentlessly criticized her appearance as well as her failed string of romantic relationships. She later becomes a pretty bad parent to Bobby Baccala’s kids, as they see through her charades easily, and after his death, the kids are stuck with her alone. All Girls Want Bad Boys:While in high school, she dated the brutal Richie Aprile, whom she is later revealed to remain attracted to despite the abusive nature of their prior relationship. While they briefly resume their relationship in Season 2,she kills him in reply to new abuse.In Season 4, she replaces Richie with the violently unstable Ralph Cifaretto.A psychiatrist makes her realize theElectra complex patternshe's locked into and guides her to break it, so she begins to look for the reverse. She quickly dumps Ralphie on some lame pretext and starts to pursue Bobby Baccalieri, aGentle Giantwho is the exact opposite of her previous type.

characters.name: Johnny Boy Soprano
characters.description: Tony's deceased father, the former captain of the Soprano crew. Abusive Parents: Along with Livia he formed one half of the trope that applied towards Tony and him ending up the way he did. Johnny Boy leaned especially towards physical abuse, intimidation, and neglect, whereas Livia was more psychologically, verbally, and emotionally abusive. Always Someone Better: He was this to Junior. Despite being the younger brother he got made first and was promoted to captain ahead of Junior, who only made capo while Johnny Boy was in prison. Throughout their entire lives he seems to have been the one calling the shots and always one step ahead of his big brother: he made more money, had more success with women, and although his family life was awful he at the very least did have a wife and kids, while Junior was a lifelong bachelor. It's a major source of Junior's insecurities and simmering resentment of Tony. Awful Wedded Life: To say that Johnny and Livia did not have a happy marriage is an understatement. Livia was a miserable woman who both verbally and physically abused him, while Johnny had no qualms about ditching her in moments of need so he could prioritize his personal desires. The only reasons they got married in the first place was thatLivia saw Johnny as her ticket out of poverty, Johnny found her physically attractive, and the cultural norms of the time meant getting married was something that was expected of them. Ax-Crazy: Easily rivaling Richie Aprile, he was frighteningly brutal and straightforward in running his business. Notice his maniacal behavior when he cut off Mr. Satriale's finger with a butcher knife for failing to pay a gambling debt.

characters.name: Barbara Soprano-Giglione
characters.description: Sister of Tony and Janice. Aloof Big Sister: Younger actually, she is quieter and more withdrawn than her loud-mouthed and dramatic older siblings. Big Little Brother: She's taller than Janice, as seen when they visit Tony in the hospital after he's shot. Catchphrase: "Will someone tell me what's going on?" Emotionless Girl: She displays little emotion when she's onscreen. ADeleted SceneinThe Many Saints of Newarkshows she was this even as a young child, as when she witnesses Tony having a panic attack and passing out, she just stares at him for several seconds before calmly yelling to Livia that Tony "had another one of his fits".

characters.name: Christopher "Chris" Moltisanti
characters.description: Tony's nephew/cousin and protege. Young and ambitious, he wants to carve a place for himself in the underworld, but his multiple flaws keep him from reaching his desired position. Accidental Murder: Once when high on heroin, Christopher slumps back on the sofa and dozes off to sleep... unaware that Adriana's dog, Cosette, is already on the couch, leading Christopher to unknowingly sit on her and break her neck. Even if the entire incident was an accident, Tony wasabsolutely lividat Christopher for allowing his recklessness to kill someone else's pet. Addiction Displacement: After he emerged from the rehab program, he seemed to develop an addiction to soda pop as a substitute, particularly Coca-Cola; it was made evident throughout the series although never addressed verbally. Addled Addict: He's pretty much unable to function properly when he's using, and when he isn't, it doesn't last long.It ultimately results in his death when he drives high and swerves off the road, critically injuring himself. Tony, deciding Chris is too much of a dangerous liability to everyone else, uses the opportunity to off him. Aesop Amnesia: No matter how many times Tony or any of the other senior mobsters tell Christopher he needs to be more responsible and can't keep goofing around when he should be earning, it never sticks.

characters.name: Richard "Dickie" Moltisanti
characters.description: Christopher's late father (and Carmela's first cousin), killed (apparently by a corrupt cop) when he was little. Anti-Villain:The Many Saints of Newarkshows that for all of his violent tendencies and prejudices, Dickie, more so than the other mobsters, struggles with the morality of the crimes they commit and tries to put just as much good into the world as the bad he does. Broken Pedestal: Christopher eventually reconciles the fact that his previously idolized father was little more than a violent junkie.Even more tragically, it turns out that he actuallywasn't. Cool Uncle: To Tony. Janice even considers him her favorite uncle. The Corrupter:The Many Saints of Newarkshows that his influence on Tony's life is what turned him into the ruthless and brutal crime boss that he is today. However, it was largely unintentional on Dickie's part and he tried to distance himself from Tony once he realized the effect he was having.Unfortunately, he's killed not long after making this decision.

characters.name: Aldo "Hollywood Dick" Moltisanti
characters.description: Dickie's father and Christopher's grandfather. Abusive Parents: Dickie tells Giuseppina that his dad used to beat him up everyday when he was a kid. Advertised Extra:Played With:Ray Liotta's presence in the trailers makes no mention of the fact that he's playing twin brothers; Aldo dies by the end of the first act by Dickie's hands and the scenes from the trailer are actually his twin brother Sally. All Girls Want Bad Boys: He justifies his domestic abuses on his partners that some women like the 'rough stuff'. This only pisses Dickie off even more that he eventuallykills his dad. Asshole Victim:His death at Dickie's hand comes after years of abusing Dickie's mother and throwing his new wife Giuseppina down some stairs.

characters.name: Joanne Blundetto-Moltisanti
characters.description: Christopher Moltisanti's mother. Aww Look They Really Do Love Each Other: While she and her son have a rather rocky relationship, both of them do care for one another. Butt-Monkey: Loses her husband when her son was an infant and much, much laterloses her son as well.On the plus side, at least she still has her grand daughter. Genre Savvy: She quickly figures Phil Leotardo is not good news. It Runs in the Family: She had problems with alcohol much like Chris's problems with drugs.

characters.name: Anthony "Tony B" Blundetto
characters.description: Cousin of Tony Soprano who is released from jail in season 5. Affably Evil: Gets along well with most of the mobsters and is generally a fairly likable sort. He's still a violent thug and a hitman, however. Animal Motifs: Although not a specific one. Janice describes him as a "fox", and Phil Leotardo frequently refers to him as a wild animaleven after his death, with Tony S being incapable of keeping him under controluntil he has to give him aMercy Killa laOld Yeller. Beware the Nice Ones: Is usually pleasant with most people, but he has a vengeful streak. Broken Pedestal: Tony S looked up to Tony B when they were younger, and he continued to idolize him once he got released from prison.Tony B's impulsive attack on the Leotardo brothers sours Tony S's perception immensely.

characters.name: Pat Blundetto
characters.description: A retired soldier of the family. Uncle of Tony Blundetto and Chris Moltisanti. Back for the Finale: He reappears in "Made in America" to visit Junior and warn Tony about Janice's schemes. Call to Agriculture: He retired from the business to live in a farm. Cool Old Guy: Well-liked by his nephews and most other mobsters. He even supports Chris' sobriety when most of the made guys disparage it. Disposing of a Body: His farm doubles as a mob graveyard, where at least three bodies are buried.

characters.name: Harpo "Hal" Soprano
characters.description: The estranged son of Janice. Butt-Monkey: The poor guy can finally say which would be worse: Having Janice as a parent or being abandoned by her and left to live on the streets. The Ghost: Never seen. Only mentioned in dialogue. On other shows, a never seen, not important to the plot child of one of the main characters seem like perfect fodder for being mentioned once and then never again but from Janice's first season all the way to her final scene in the series, Hal is referenced, making him a definitive part of Janice's character. Long-Lost Relative: He’s not mentioned often, except when Tony wants to piss off Janice, and Janice appears to have totally lost track of him over the years. Tragically, the family as a whole seems to ignore his existence and never make attempts to reach him, despite Tony claiming he’s “the boy’s uncle.” Named After Somebody Famous: Discussed/mocked. He's not named after Harpo Marx but after the song "Harpo's Blues."

characters.name: Ercole "Eckley" Soprano
characters.description: Brother of Corrado Jr. and Johnny Soprano, uncle of Anthony. Born in the Wrong Century: Junior laments that had Eckley been born later, the family would have had a lot more resources to help him with his disability and he might have been able to be a contributing member of society. Instead, they had no choice but to leave him to live in an institution as there were no other options at the time. Brainless Beauty: According to Junior, he was handsome and fit, but he was mentally disabled. Dumb Muscle: Junior says he was strong like a bull, and handsome like George Raft. The Ghost: He's never seen.

characters.name: Hugo "Hugh" and Mary De Angelis
characters.description: Beware the Nice Ones: Hugh is generally a laid-back guy, but at Livia's funeral he goes on an angry rant about how horrible the woman was and ignores his wife's protests about it.He also takes zero shit off of Carmela when she accuses him of looting her spec house construction site. He also takes zero shit off of Carmela when she accuses him of looting her spec house construction site. But Not Too White: Inverted, when Meadow was born, Mary was disappointed by the dark skin tone of her granddaughter. Butt-Monkey: Hugh doesn't get much respect from his family and suffers a series of illnesses and injuries. Construction Is Awesome: Hugh built the amazing Sopranos house, one of the few things in their lives that is never a subject of contention. Not so much in the modern times with Carmela's spec house, which comes close to a dead end due to Hugh lack of familiarity with the new regulations.

characters.name: Tom Giglione
characters.description: Husband of Barbara Soprano. Even the Loving Hero Has Hated Ones: Tom's aNice Guyto everyone in the Sopranos family with the notable exception ofLivia. He flat out refused to let her live with him and Barbara when she brought up the subject and later supports Carmela and Hugh when theySpeak Ill of the Deadat her wake. The Generic Guy: Receives absolutely no characterization. Happily Married: As far as the series can show, he and Barbara enjoy a very calm life away from her family's drama, in contrast to the lives of her older siblings and their spouses/partners. Hufflepuff House: He's the husband of one of the Soprano siblings, yet makes only a few appearances.

characters.name: Brian Cammarata
characters.description: Carmela's cousin and a financial advisor. Brick Joke: Borrows Tony's power drill in season four. Tony eventually forgets what happened to it and has to give Tony Blundetto a rudimentary drill in season five. Damn, It Feels Good to Be a Gangster!: He's clearly seduced by the flashy aspects of the criminal life and likes to casually hang around with the professional thugs. Evil Genius: Tony's fiscal advisor and the brains behind the HUD scam. Morality Pet: Initially, Tony does Brian favors to earn praise from an upstanding civilian. As Brian gets drawn into Tony's criminal lifestyle, this role deteriorates, and Tony loses interest in this friendship.

characters.name: In general
characters.description: Affably Evil:ZigZagged. On their best days, they are completely civil and cordial when they can be, as long as you don't piss them off, aren't in on the game, and aren't an informant. Allegorical Character: TheDiMeoscan be read as a very clear allegoryfor the Silent and Baby Boomer generations trapped in a 21st-century worldwhere the American Dream, traditional American prosperity, authority, sense of community, and traditional American male roles no longer mean anything in the face of an increasingly globalized and individualistic world.Although in the case of the Baby Boomers (a group which Tony and those around his age fall into) it's a bit moreDownplayed. This generation can be seen as more of a bridge between these eras rather than disconnected from the modern era. Indeed, there are quite a few aspects of the modern era that they welcome, even if they talk in more traditionalistic terms sometimes. Although in the case of the Baby Boomers (a group which Tony and those around his age fall into) it's a bit moreDownplayed. This generation can be seen as more of a bridge between these eras rather than disconnected from the modern era. Indeed, there are quite a few aspects of the modern era that they welcome, even if they talk in more traditionalistic terms sometimes. Always Someone Better: They claim to rule north Jersey, but the family is small potatoes next to the might of any of the five New York families from across the Hudson River (especially the Lupertazzis). Ambiguous Situation: There is quite a bit of ambiguity about much of the history of the family, particularly in regards toDiMeohimself. It's not made that clear to what extent the regular characters knew him and what they thought of him (and he of them). His actual name gets only a solitary mention in the whole series, and that is during a news report on Jackie Sr's death four episodes in.

characters.name: Ercole "Eckley"DiMeo
characters.description: Longtime head of theDiMeocrime family. Artifact Name: In-universe: theDiMeoCrime Family, of which the Soprano crew is a major part, still bears ErcoleDiMeo's name, even though he's been in prison for more than a decade, and no one named "DiMeo" has any part in running the family. The family's name is sometimes written as the "DiMeo/Soprano Family" to reflect Junior and Tony's tenure. Authority in Name Only: Officially, he's still the boss of the crime family that bears his name. But since he's locked up in federal prison for life with no way to fulfill any of his duties, his subordinates take up the role of acting boss. The Cameo: He makes a quick walkthrough appearance at Lino Bonpensiero's funeral inThe Many Saints of Newark, never exactly shown in detail. The Don: Founder and hierarchical boss of theDiMeofamily.

characters.name: Giacomo "Jackie" Aprile, Sr.
characters.description: The acting boss of theDiMeofamily at the start of the series. The Ace: From what little we see of him and from what we see of his successors, it's clear Jackie was the perfect leader for the family. He was able to keep Tony's fierce temper in check and a pro at diplomatically resolving troubles, effortlessly engineering a truce between Tony and Junior after Chris and Brendan hit one of Jun's protected trucks. Affably Evil: Despite being a ruthless mob boss, he is depicted as being very friendly and diplomatic in his dealings with others, even while suffering from terminal cancer. Additionally, even after being confined to the hospital and dying from aforementioned cancer, Tony and the other capos within theDiMeocrime family speak fondly of his fair and charismatic leadership. Benevolent Boss: Seemed to genuinely care about his men, as shown when he offers to lend some money to Pussy. The Don: Boss of the Jersey crew at the start of the series.

characters.name: Silvio Manfred Dante
characters.description: Tony's most trusted advisor and right-hand man. Affably Evil: Despite being a ruthless mobster, he is a good person to hang out with. This, alongside with his level-headedness and ability to rein in Tony, makes him the most widely respected of all the members of Tony's inner-circle by the family's members and associates.When he's taken out by the Lupertazzis, all of the men take time to visit him at the hospital even with the war going on and become openly resentful towards Tony when it appears he's not doing the same. Ambiguous Situation: What role did Silvio play in Tony's unofficial crew in the '80s? Ralph described Silvio as his, Tony, and Jackie's contemporary, implying he's an upstart just like them. However,The Many Saints of Newarkdepicts Silvio as having been an established soldier of theDiMeoCrime Family since the '60s, raising questions about what a senior Mafia member would be doing with what would be seen as bunch of two-bit thugs. Bait the Dog: In many other works, one might think Silvio's hatred of a pedophile coach, his adoring love of his daughter whom he lavishly calls "The Principessa" and his levelheaded sense of honor would lead to aNoble Demonwith standards who protects women. Silvio is an abusive, misogynist pimp who uses the girls at the Bada Bing as terrorized prostitutes to bring in income with the pretense of owing him money. He sees no contradiction between any of this. Berserk Button:Gambling - specifically, when Lady Luckturns against him.It would be fair to say that almost anyone in the crime family would be outraged by one of their own becomingThe Molefor the FBI, and wouldn't hesitate to execute the traitor. But Silvio stands out in this regard. He personally participates in the execution of at least three FBI informants,Jimmy Altieri, Big Pussy and Adriana.And each time his facial expression and lowered voice conveys intense fury over what he considersthe worst kind of betrayalthere is.

characters.name: Peter Paul "Paulie Walnuts" Gualtieri
characters.description: A long-time soldier of the Soprano crew, later caporegime, and finally underboss in theDiMeoCrime Family. Affably Evil: Paulie is often cracking jokes and usually has an upbeat, chipper personality, but he's quick to switch to threats and murderous rage. Ax-Crazy: Paulie is highly impulsive and homicidal. "Pine Barrens" famously sees his inability to let go of what was anextremelyminor slightset up the whole episode's central conflict. As a result, what was just a simple job of picking up a loan payment escalates to attempted murder and finally to him and Chris getting hopelessly lost in the woods where they almost get killed by exposure (while almost killing each other too). And just check out some of his psychotic facial expressions. Bad People Abuse Animals: Downplayed. He isn't a big fan of the cat who shows up in Satriale's at the end of the series but he doesn't do anything awful to him beyond shooing him out of the room. Upon hearing that Christopher caused the death of Adrianna's dog, Paulie asks if it was barking. Bait the Dog: He stands up for Vito initially, calling the rumors malicious slander and refusing to believe it without actual proof. But when the truth comes out after Finn's testimony, he's out for blood like no one else, second only to Carlo, and questioning Tony's leadership in the process.

characters.name: Bobby "Baccala" Baccalieri
characters.description: A rising member of the Soprano crew, who later marries Janice Soprano. Affably Evil: Bobby is possibly the nicest mobster in the entire show. He’s a devoted family man, is generally very passive and shy to the point of nearButt-Monkeystatus (a reputation he manages to shake by the last few seasons), and is not very aggressive compared to his friends. This is somewhat Downplayed in the final few episodes.After carrying out his first whackinghe becomes less friendly and cuddly compared to earlier. All for Nothing: Bobby gradually climbs his way up the ranks of the crime family through simple loyalty and diligence, and is the most earnest caretaker of Junior, even more so than Junior's own biological family. He ends up as one of the underbosses, and leading choice to become Tony's successor as acting boss afterTony kills Christopher, only tobe suddenly murdered as the first major casualty of aMob War. Even worse, Junior's growing dementia means he's completely forgotten who Bobby is and will never be able to repay Bobby's kindness, his kids are now trapped withJaniceas their primary guardian, the guests at his funeral take far more interest in the afterparty buffet than Bobby himself, and his killers end up beingKarma Houdinisdue to mob politics (at best, Tony makes them pay reparations for Bobby's death, and only because Bobby was married to his sister). Anti-Villain: The most sympathetic and most innocent mobster in the series by a wide margin. Anyone Can Die: He's married to Janice and a large part of the show,then dies extremely suddenly later.

characters.name: Pasquale "Patsy" Parisi
characters.description: An enforcer introduced in Season 2. He is also the family's accountant. Affably Evil: One of the more pleasant gangsters, and, aside from a beating and intimidation,is rarely involved with violence. Even when he's threatening to kill someone (likeGloria) he delivers his threats in a calm, friendly tone of voice. The Alcoholic: Spends an episodedrowning his sorrows over his brother's death. Gigi mentions him "getting into the booze very heavily" and needing to be helped off the bar floor.Averted, seemingly, for the rest of the series, as he becomes a loyal underling to Tony and apparently puts his (understandable) grievance against Tony aside. Alliterative Name:Pasquale "Patsy"Parisi. Angsty Surviving Twin: He's devastated after his talkativetwin, Philly, gets killed on Tony's order.

characters.name: Salvatore "Big Pussy" Bonpensiero
characters.description: Tony's best friend and a long-time member of the Soprano crew. Affably Evil: Azig-zagbetween this andFaux Affably Evil. Despite being a hardened criminal, he's a benevolent mentor to the hotheaded Christopher Moltisanti, whose easygoing personality belies his unwavering loyalty to Tony Soprano. He also serves as AJ's sponsor for his confirmation, offering some adult advice. However, though a loving father, he's a ruthless mobster, assassin andat times an abusive husband. Alas, Poor Villain:Gets one at the end of "D Girl" at AJ's Communion party.His last moments by the end of Season 2. Alone on a boat with his closest friends, they soon turn on him and confront him about his status as an informant for the FBI. He initially tries to face his inevitable murder with some dignity, but is unceremoniously gunned down after realizing that there was no way out for him. Gets one at the end of "D Girl" at AJ's Communion party. His last moments by the end of Season 2. Alone on a boat with his closest friends, they soon turn on him and confront him about his status as an informant for the FBI. He initially tries to face his inevitable murder with some dignity, but is unceremoniously gunned down after realizing that there was no way out for him.

characters.name: Furio Giunta
characters.description: An enforcer from Italy who joins theDiMeofamily in Season 2, brought in as part of a "men-for-cars" deal with the NeapolitanCamorra.noteFun fact: in Napoli, the Camorraarethe waste-management business. Seriously; their handling of the city's municipal waste hascaused serious environmental issues. The Ace: Furio is by far the most effective enforcer in theDiMeofamily, thanks to his toughness and no-nonsense personality. It's probably not a coincidence that after he flees New Jersey, the group finds itself struggling against the Lupertazzis. Affably Evil: He's very polite and cultured in addition to being a violent thug who has no qualms with beating women and children. Furio can go from laid-back to vicious in seconds as the job demands. Beware the Quiet Ones: While he acts calm and reserved, he has certain moments of violence throughout the series. The Big Guy: He's 6'2" and the most physically formidable member of Tony's crew.

characters.name: Eugene Pontecorvo
characters.description: An enforcer in the Cifaretto crew. Alas, Poor Villain: He's a stone-cold killer and a violent thug.And yet, there's something tragic about his suicide. Ambiguously Gay: Implied on several occasions by other characters,including the secretly homosexual Vito. A Death in the Limelight:Finally gets some screentime where he looks like he might be the new mole threat to Tony. He kills himself about five minutes after we find this out. Demoted to Extra: Robert Funaro is credited in the opening titles in season three, so Eugene is clearly seen as a major character by the writers at that point (or perhaps Funaro just had a good agent), but is then relegated to the closing credits. The fact that he gets made alongside Christopher in his first appearance gives an indication of prominence, but it never really materializes.

characters.name: Benito "Benny" Fazio Jr.
characters.description: A young enforcer and friend of Chris Moltisanti who gradually rises up to become a high-ranking soldier in theDiMeofamily. The Ace: Benny gets trusted with a lot of tasks and, aside from maybe his fighting prowess, is one of the more competent young gangsters on the rise in theDiMeofamily. His staying power and persistence is especially impressive, no matter how many times he is beaten.Artie:"I'm just another victim of Benny Fazio,criminal mastermind." Affably Evil: One of the nicest guys in the Soprano crew, but he's brutal when he needs to be. Ascended Extra: Is a background character in Season 3 and 4, and then rises in importance around Season 5 and 6 once he gets made. Blatant Lies: When confronted by Artie over conducting credit card fraud in his restaurant, he gives this halfhearted excuse as justification for his actions: "I was gonna cut you in, but now you're acting stupid!"

characters.name: Peter "Bissell"LaRosa
characters.description: A would-be soldier in Paulie's crew. The Apprentice: A rising hitman who makes his bones during the show and doubles as a doorman. The Generic Guy: His role is to further demonstrate the growing number of new blood filling up theDiMeoFamily's ranks.

characters.name: Mikey Palmice
characters.description: Junior's right-hand man at the start of the series. Affably Evil: Downplayed, but he seems to lionize "old school" mafiosos like Junior and the result is aslightlymore refined class of gangster. He seems like an okay guy to be around in general, provided you don't hassle him constantly (Tony) and he doesn't have orders to kill you (an occasion he'll dip into full-blownFaux Affably Evilfor). He's also a bit over-enthusiastic when he gets going on a topic and unthinkingly lays on the gory details too thick and fast for some.Jackie Sr.: Thank God he left. He's a nice guy but he's like the grim fucking reaper. Ain't Too Proud to Beg: Spends his last moments yelling "Please!" over and over again and insisting that it was Junior, not him, that murdered Brendan Filone. Asshole Victim: A cold-blooded killer and all-aroundJerkasswhose final moments are begging for mercy as Paulie and Christopher pump him full of lead. Horrible way to go, but he absolutely had it coming. Belligerent Sexual Tension: Trades insults and barbs with his wife in every scene they have together, but there's a definite flirtatious element to it.

characters.name: Philly "Spoons" Parisi
characters.description: Enforcer and Patsy's younger twin brother introduced in the Season 2 premiere. Alliterative Name:PhillipParisi. Though the fact that his nickname was "Spoons" means it was in play to a lesser degree than his twin, Patsy. Loose Lips: While Tony's motivation for ordering the hit on Philly was mainly political in nature, as he was one of the likely candidates to ascend to boss after Junior's incarceration, it is implied that it was also at least partially because Tony also resented Philly's gossipy nature ona personal level, blaming him for starting the (factual) rumor that he attempted to strangle his mother. Small Role, Big Impact: His death made Patsy resentful towards Tony.This might or might not have resulted in his assassination or imprisonment. We Hardly Knew Ye: Philly only appears in two episodes, and in the second one he solely appears in a dream sequence. Additionaly, a flashback of Gigi killing him is shown in Season 3 premiere.

characters.name: Robert "Baccala" Baccalieri, Sr.
characters.description: An aging but brutalDiMeohitman and father of Bobby Baccala. Affably Evil: He can engage in banter with his son and friends, then gleefully enjoy sadistically murdering his targets the next moment. He also has a reputation as the "Terminator" for the mob. Alas, Poor Villain: As awful a man as Baccala is, seeing this reportedly “proud man” and feared mob enforcer reduced to a walking asthma attack who can barely stand up is quite pitiable. Asthma Peril: He suffers coughing fits due to advancing lung cancer from heavy smoking over decades and always carries around an inhaler.He ends up meeting his end when he suffers another such fit while driving, drops his inhaler out of reach, passes out, and crashes into a pole, instantly killing himself. Ax-Crazy: He clearly enjoys his job.

characters.name: Burt Gervasi
characters.description: A soldier and Carlo Gervasi's cousin. Introduced late in Season 5. Ascended Extra: Has a single apperance in Season 5 "In Camelot", becominga background characterand more important in the final season. A Death in the Limelight:His one important storyline happens near the very end of the series, in which he is murdered for treason. Dumb Muscle: Like his cousin Carlo, he is not overtly stupiduntil he asininely attempts to make Silvio defect to New York, but gives off the impression of not being very sharp overall either, possessing a rather lethargic mind. Rank Up: Burt and Gerry Torciano become a "made man" for their respective families at the same time, and have a shared celebration afterwards.

characters.name: Walden Belfiore
characters.description: A reliable, subdued Soprano hitman from the Altieri crew, notable for committing the final confirmed murder of the series. 11th-Hour Ranger: Shows up in the last few episodes during a crunch time in the rivalry between New Jersey and New York and ends upbeing the one who takes out Phil Leotardo. Affably Evil: Quite kind and relaxed for a man we see in the finale is a cold-blooded hitman who ruthlessly and unflinchingly guns down a mob boss in front of his wife and grandchildren while wearing a determinedDeath Glare. Ambiguously Related: He shares the maiden name of Big Pussy's wife Angie, hinting at a possible familial relation. Badass Longcoat: Wears a black one during the finale.

characters.name: Lino "Buddha" Bonpensiero
characters.description: A soldier in Johny Boy's crew and the father of "Big Pussy" Bonpensiero. In-Series Nickname: Dubbed "Buddha" on account of his large-size, reminiscent of depictions of the Chinese buddhist monk Budai, who is often mistaken for the original Buddha.

characters.name: Annalisa Zucca
characters.description: The exuberant and de facto boss of the Neapolitan Camorra. Affably Evil: The actual mob boss of the Camorra, but she is extremely well-mannered and polite, especially when compared to Tony himself. Beneath the Mask: Annalisa is shown to be thereal brains behind the Camorra, but deliberately passes herself off as Vittorio's caretaker in order to diffuse suspicion. She's later shown to be a tough, capable woman who can more than hold her own, and tells Tony that her brothers all died via in-family fighting while she excelled by playing a part. Bunny-Ears Lawyer: A shrewd businesswoman who has a quirky superstition; she burns her nail clippings and cut hair to prevent them from falling into her enemies' hands and being used to curse her. Brainy Brunette: She has a good grasp of English and can manage an actual Italian crime family with ease.

characters.name: The Tailors
characters.description: A trio of seasoned hitmen from Naples. Genius Bruiser: For both their hits, they use tactics to put their targets off their guard and get their hands away from their guns. They're quite effective at what they do, although they get bad information at one point and mistakenly kill the wrong man. Mistaken Identity: They kill the father of Phil's mistress instead of Phil because the two grey foxes look very alike. Professional Killer: Hired to kill Rusty Millio and Phil Leotardo, with mixed results. Replacement Goldfish: Roberto replaces Salvatore as Italos getaway driver in the hit against Phil Leotardo, in which the wrong man is killed.

characters.name: Slava Malevsky
characters.description: A Russian mobster and business partner of Tony. Affably Evil: He's very personable and friendly with Tony, quick to open his heart to lament the sorry state of his dear friend Valery. The Don: Of the Russian mob. The Mafiya: Head of the Russian mob. Red Oni, Blue Oni: The calm and friendly Blue to Valery's brash and alcoholic Red.

characters.name: Valery
characters.description: A Russian mook who proves to be too much for Christopher and Paulie in "Pine Barrens". The Alcoholic: He routinely abuses drugs andalcohol. Ax-Crazy: It is established from the beginning that he is a sullen, volatile and violent man, even ifit was Paulie who caused him to lose his temper in the first place. Bullying a Dragon: He only had to pay Paulie Silvio's money, but Paulie escalates the conflict to a point of no return. The Dragon: Served as Slava's closest comrade during the Chechen War, saving his life multiple times.

characters.name: Herman "Hesh" Rabkin
characters.description: An old Jewish business associate of theDiMeofamily, and a good friend of Tony. Affably Evil: He's charming and amicable despite being involved in some unsavory criminal activities. Alter Kocker: An older Jewish man who peppers his speech with Yiddish. Berserk Button: Hesh agrees that Native Americans were slaughtered unjustly and is initially supportive of the anti-Columbus protests. But when a Cuban friend says that Columbus was as bad as Hitler, Hesh bristles and accuses him of trivializing the Holocaust, causing the two men to nearly come to blows. Cool Old Guy: In anAffably Evilsort of way.

characters.name: Peter "Beansie" Gaeta
characters.description: A former associate of Richie Aprile involved in his drug operations. Bittersweet Ending: He becomes a paraplegic thanks to Richie Aprile, but is able to leave the mob behind. In the end, he secures a comfortable position in Florida and has a decent relationship with his wife. Career-Ending Injury: Is allowed to retire after Richie Aprile prevents him from ever walking again, a rarity for anyone involved in the life. Cut Lex Luthor a Check: Subverted. He started off as a low level associate directly involved in the mob's rackets who found more success as a restauranteur acting as a silent partner to help them launder money. A Lighter Shade of Black: He's not directly involved in the mob. Instead, he works with Tony as a partner by using his pizza shops (which are otherwise totally legit) to help launder money.

characters.name: Jasons Gervasi and Parisi
characters.description: Best friends and sons of Carlo Gervasi and Patsy Parisi, both named Jason. Bait the Dog: Introduced as happier counterparts to A.J. Seeing their apparently functional lives, Tony pushes A.J. to befriend them. They genuinely bond with him and things seem to take a turn for the better, but then they start roping him into their violent activities. Dirty Coward: Act as a pair of hotshots and violent pricks whenever their similarly thuggish frat guy friends are watching their back and generally like to prey on those who are weaker than them. These traits make it quite obvious that the two of them are nothing more than pathetic, wannabe gangsters as their fathers are more than capable of holding their own. Heterosexual Life-Partners: A duo of brats who are rarely seen without each other. Karma Houdini: Neither of them get any onscreen comeuppance for their actions which includes torturing a gambler with sulfuric acid or Jason G getting arrested for dealing drugs considering his father is about to testify in order to get him off the hook, further adding to their already unlikeable nature.

characters.name: Jackie Aprile Jr.
characters.description: Son of Jackie Aprile, the late boss of theDiMeocrime family. In pursuit of his ambition to follow in his father's footsteps, he increasingly becomes a nuisance for Tony Soprano after he forms his own gang and sets out to make a name for himself. Acquired Situational Narcissism: Having a high-ranking father and uncle in the mafia is a huge source of his entitlement. The fact that he was nudged toward the lifestyle byhis uncleRichiedidn't help either. Ain't Too Proud to Beg:Rings Tony to beg him for forgiveness after the card game bloodbath. Tony shows him none. Allegorical Character: Many people try to use a deceased family member's legacy to their advantage. In the case of Jackie Jr, though, it also seems to fit in with the general theme of theDiMeocrime family being past its best. Jackie Sr was a leading and well-respected member during its better days, and Jackie Jr is notably useless and inept, representing the idea that the glory days for the family are over. Ambition Is Evil: His desire to rise to the top of theDiMeocrime family while running roughshod over its rules and hierarchy.

characters.name: Paul "Little Paulie" Germani
characters.description: Nephew of Paulie Gualtieri. Actually Pretty Funny: Manages to dole out a few funny zingers. Butt-Monkey: Besides Georgie the bartender, he is one of the most abused characters on the show. He gets hit with a bottle on 2 separate occasions and eventually thrown out of a window. Crouching Moron, Hidden Badass: Was actually pretty scary in a scene where he had to intimidate and beat up J.T. Dolan. The Determinator: Keeps looking forPhileven while having to wear a neck brace and crutches.

characters.name: LouDiMaggioand the Atwell Avenue Boys
characters.description: An old crew of brutal hitmen recommended to Tony for a whacking by Junior. Actor Allusion: They decapitated a guy named Tommy Neri with a hacksaw. Frank is played by Richard Bright, who famously portrayed Al Neri inThe Godfather. Ax-Crazy: They are effective but sadistic, completely terrifying mercenaries. One of them beat one treacherous mobster and his wife to death with a baseball bat, earning Lou's nickname "DiMaggio". They also decapitated a man with a hacksaw while he was still alive. Blind Seer: Invoked by Lou, who is blind, when he asks Chris if he's into drugs. Lou was actually just asking if the Soprano family was involved in drug running, something he is fundamentally opposed to. Cloud Cuckoo Lander: ADarker and Edgiervariation. The youngest member of their crew is unnervingly friendly and enthusiastic. Upon meeting Christopher Moltisanti, he remarks that his name is also Chris. Seeing a picture of Johnny Sack at his birthday, he remarks that it's his birthday as well.

characters.name: Brendan Filone
characters.description: A young associate, friend, and partner in crime of Christopher Moltisanti. Addled Addict: He likes to portray himself as aFunctional Addict, but even Brendan admits that his meth addiction affects his thinking skills. Ain't Too Proud to Beg: Asks forgiveness from Tony for repeated errors. Ambition Is Evil: Attempts to climb in the ranks too quickly. Asshole Victim: He's a totalJerkasswho mocks Jackie Aprile's cancer and creepily hits on underage Hunter. It's hard to be mad at Junior for having him killed, especially as Brendan robbed the truck after Jackie generously gave him a pass the first time.

characters.name: Matthew Bevilaqua
characters.description: A young associate of Chris Moltisanti. Ain't Too Proud to Beg:When Tony gives Matt aPre-Mortem One-Liner, he cries out for his mother before begging Tony not to shoot him. Alas, Poor Villain:As unlikeable as Matt was, his pointlessly cruel and drawn-out death is hard to watch. Tony, who orchestrated the whole thing, is even shown to be haunted by it later on. Ambiguously Gay: While Furio's remark was probably a joke, getting high with your roommate/friend in your underwear while having your clothes laying around does raise questions. He also seems to be a bit more upset than might be expected for a mob associate afterSean is shot dead by Christopher. Arson, Murder, and Jaywalking: Matt tells Christopher that he and Sean would love to do errands for Tony. The two ideas he specifically mentions are assassinations and picking up his shirts from the dry cleaners.

characters.name: Sean Gismonte
characters.description: Associate of Chris Moltisanti and best friend of Matt Bevilaqua. Ambiguously Gay: While Furio's remark was probably a joke, getting high with your roommate/friend in your underwear while having your clothes laying around does raise questions. Boom, Headshot!:Gets killed instantly with a clean shot through the head. Brainless Beauty: One of the better looking male characters in the series, but certainly not one of the more intelligent. Bring My Brown Pants: Can often be found shitting on the floor due to nerves during safe-cracking, while Chris and Matt do the work.

characters.name: Fabian "Febby" Petrulio
characters.description: A former soldier in theDiMeofamily who turned federal informant. Ain't Too Proud to Beg: Even as he's being garrotted by Tony. Asshole Victim: To ensure that we don't feeltoobad about Tony killing him, he's seen peddling drugs to teenagers. He also shows no hesitation or scruples when he attempts to snipe Tony in front of his daughter, only canceling the shot because of the sudden appearance of other motel guests and wanting no witnesses or complications. Blatant Lies: Lies through his teeth in a vain attempt to save his life, saying he left Tony and Meadow alone due to his conscience and not the presence of witnesses. Dirty Coward: In addition to having become an informant to save his own skin, he tries to shoot Tony from behind, even with Meadow present, and later tries desperately to beg for his life when Tony finally gets him.

characters.name: William "Petite" Clayborn and Rasheen Ray
characters.description: Two small-time criminals commissioned by Junior Soprano to kill Tony in the first season. Boom, Headshot!: Petite Clayborn's death, in slow motion. Car Fu: Their altercation with Tony is comprised mostly of this. Gangbangers: A couple of black street gangsters. I Just Shot Marvin in the Face: Rasheen accidentally shoots Petite in the head while aiming for Tony in a moving car.

characters.name: Patrick Parisi
characters.description: The other son of Patsy Parisi, and boyfriend of Meadow. Always Save the Girl: When Coco harasses Meadow, Patrick stands up to her and has the balls to get ready to have a go with a much larger and stronger Coco in her defense. Amoral Attorney: A mob lawyer in the making. Character Development: Offscreen. Meadow reconnects with him and tells her parents that he has changed. Dating What Daddy Hates: Meadow's parents are clearly not amused that Meadow is going to marry a wiseguy associate.

characters.name: Ronald Zellman
characters.description: New Jersey assemblyman in bed with the mob. Ascended Extra: Appears briefly in Season 3 before gaining prominence in Season 4. Corrupt Politician: Tony's equal partner in a majorreal estate scam. The Fixer: His position in local government comes with a lot of connections which prove useful to Tony. Foe Cooties: Played with; initially Tony appears unaffected by his dating of Irina and gives his blessing, but eventually Zellman gets viciously beaten up for having a relationship with the former comare of Tony.

characters.name: Richard "Dick" Barone
characters.description: Owner of Barone sanitation, a front business for the Soprano crew. Corrupt Corporate Executive: Downplayed. He's shown to engage in small-time corruption like price fixing with the other garbage hauling companies, and he's in bed with the mob, but that's just the cost of doing business in New Jersey. Otherwise his business is fairly legit. Due to the Dead: His funeral congregates a high number of mafiosos, despite not being a made man or a relative. Family Business: Inherited by his son, who is not interested in playing ball with the mob until Paulierenews the arrangement. Ripped from the Headlines: Partly based onThomas Milo, a garbage hauler cracked down by Giuliani in the 90s.

characters.name: Neil Mink
characters.description: Amoral Attorney: A traditional mob lawyer. Aside from anything else, Tony basically tells him that he's planning to take out a witness and he pretends not to have heard him. Consummate Professional: Manages to constantly be on-call for Tony whenever he needs him. Neil even gets him off of a gun charge and gives him some motivational words despite confirming thatCarlo turned witness. He also refuses to charge Tony if he doesn't think he's had to really work for it. Dirty Old Man: Can't help but stare at the topless Bing dancers on camera while giving Tony some legal news. Dude, Not Funny!: Unusually for someone usually so careful with his words and in how he interacts, he decides to crack a joke about Tony's situation in "All Due Respect". Tony had just escaped from Johnny Sack's house and was paranoid about the Feds coming after him next. Understandably, Tony calls Mink out on the bad timing of the joke. Minor Major Character: The lawyer to a perpetually conflicted mob boss protagonist is inherently a heavyweight role, yet he only appears sparingly in 8 episodes total.

characters.name: Harold "Mel" Melvoin
characters.description: Amoral Attorney: A traditional and very expensive mob lawyer. Last-Name Basis: Unlike Tony (who often refers to Neil Mink by his first name), Junior almost exclusively uses 'Melvoin' or 'Mel' rather than 'Harold'. Put on a Bus: Doesn't appear after Season 5, partly due to the decline in his own health and partly due toJunior being incarcerated in a mental facility after shooting Tony. Speech Impediment: Suffers a stroke that affects his ability to speak. Gets fired afterward by Junior.

characters.name: Dante "Buddha" Greco
characters.description: An associate of the family and one of Tony's bodyguards and drivers after being shot by Junior and during the war with New York. Affably Evil: A friendly, subdued, introspective man who loves and takes care of his mother, despite his criminal occupation. Badass Biker: Was introduced as one before he grew closer to the family and started working for Tony directly. Evil Laugh: Seems to have one from Christopher's drunken point of view, when everyone appears to be laughing mockingly at him at a party. Hidden Depths: Takes care of his mother who is suffering from Lupus, and wistfully suggests that he could have had an honest career as a medical worker or caregiver, and might in another life. He also dances with Rosalie Aprile at the wedding of Johnny Sack's daughter when a song for married couples plays because Rosalie is a widow.

characters.name: James "Murmur" Zancone
characters.description: Friend, AA sponsor, and criminal associate of Christopher Moltisanti. Actually Pretty Funny: Has a pig joke that manages to make Tony laugh. Tony even uses it himself in a following episode. The Consigliere: To Chris when it comes to sobriety. In a rare departure from theToxic Friend Influenceinveterate to Mafia circles, he actually gives Chris good advice and functions as a more reliable sponsor than JT despite his criminality. Had Chris turned to Murmur rather than JT when he hit his nadir inWalk Like A Man,the consequences would probably not have been fatal. Embarrassing Nickname: The nickname "Murmur" comes from him having a heart murmur as a kid. Evil Genius: An expert at forging documents.

characters.name: Perry "Muscles Marinara" Annunziata
characters.description: A bodybuilder brought in as Tony's driver and bodyguard after recovering from getting shot by Junior. Dumb Muscle: He's not quite bright. Gentle Giant: When he's not angered, he's actually quite respectful and gentle. Hair-Trigger Temper: He's noted as being quick to anger and respond with violence. Manchild: Despite his age and size he confides in his parents like a kid trying to fit in at school.Perry:My mom says I should count 10, but I never remember.

characters.name: Corky Caporale
characters.description: A first-generation Italian heroin junkie, friend, and associate of Christopher. His fluency in the Italian language means he is generally the bottom-level go-between withfriends from the other side. Covert Pervert: Hides out in a porn store while the Italians do the Leotardo hit. Dark and Troubled Past: Briefly mentions that he was born in Italy, and is shown to be wary of native Italian mobsters, for unspecified reasons. Functional Addict: Though something of a bottom-feeder. Spanner in the Works: In the penultimate episode, Corky acts as a go-between with the Italian assassins in the hit on Phil.After the hitmen mistakenly murder Phil's goomah's father instead, they briefly mention to Corky that she referred to the target as "Daddy" in Ukrainian. Corky, in a porn store at the time, thinks nothing of this. His mistake results in Bobby's death and Silvio's coma.

characters.name: Ahmed and Muhammad
characters.description: Muslim associates of Christopher. Ambiguous Situation: It's never confirmed whether they're allied with terrorists, but doing financial scams for the mob and asking Chris for Tec-9s doesn't help their case. Conflict Killer: Islamic terrorism becomes an important part of the equation in thecomplex relationshipbetween the FBI/Tony/Phil. Those Two Guys: Become this amongst the Bing in the last season.

characters.name: Gennaro "Little Pussy" Malanga
characters.description: Junior's former associate from the pilot. The Ghost: Is never seen outside of brief five second news footage in first episode, where he is played by an uncredited actor. Significant Name Overlap: Hesh initially assumes that Junior is going to whack Pussy Bonpensiero.Tony:You think he's gonna fuck with Big Pussy? My Pussy? Small Role, Big Impact: Despite his lack of proper screentime, his conflict with Junior is quite relevant twice:First of all, Junior's attempt to kill him forced Tony to burn down the original Vesuvio in order to protect Artie's business, which nearly destroyed their friendship.Then, in Season 6,severely senile Junior confuses Tony for Little Pussy and shoots him, which causes Corrado's falling out with pretty much everyone and a severeSuccession Crisisin the mafia. First of all, Junior's attempt to kill him forced Tony to burn down the original Vesuvio in order to protect Artie's business, which nearly destroyed their friendship.

characters.name: Debbie
characters.description: The madame of a high-end brothel used by theDiMeofamily and other corrupt Jersey figures. High-Class Call Girl: Much more well-kept and professional than others in that line of work. Hooker with a Heart of Gold: She was the romantic confidante of Vin Makazian who gave him emotional support. It's implied that she had genuine feelings for him. Sex God: Not surprising given her profession."She rides better than Willie Shoemaker."

characters.name: Michele "Feech"LaManna
characters.description: An old Mustache Pete released from prison in Season 5. Plays abrief, but memorable roleas one of the new capos in theDiMeofamily before quickly getting on Tony's nerves. He became a Made Man in Italy and came to the US in the 50s. Affably Evil: When he's in a good mood, Feech is funny, grandfatherly, goofy, and a good person to spend time with. Additionally, after Tony confronts him about being behind the car theft, he politely apologizes and says that he'll learn. Whether he's sincere or notis left up to the viewer's interpretation. However,when he's in a bad mood... Alas, Poor Villain: His final scene is a bus ride back to prison, and it's fairly somber in spite of Feech's actions. Ambiguous Situation: It's unclear whether Feech was planning or at least contemplating a power struggle with Tony, or if he would have likely remained loyal to Tony with a few minor slights. We'll probably never know. Ax-Crazy: When he's in a bad mood, hisHair-Trigger Temperand violent nature are genuinely terrifying. DisturbinglyTruth in Television: he belongs to that old breed of mobster from theThe '50sand'70swho used to be comparatively less restrained in brutality.

characters.name: Richard "Richie" Aprile, Sr.
characters.description: ADiMeocrime family member released from prison at the start of Season 2. Affably Evil:ZigZagged. A completely ruthless mobster who behaves in a completely civil and polite manner toward civilians and the families of those involved in the mafia business. SeePet the Dogbelow.Truth in Television, as the vast majority of old-school mobsters, however violent and ruthless they were, kept civilians and children out of the reach of their business dealings. The Aggressive Drug Dealer: Cuts into Tony's garbage routes to sell cocaine at a time when the mob is trying to break away from crimes that will draw FBI attention and drops into aTranquil Furywhen told off by his boss. Richie's drug dealing however is more to show how bad the Dimeo's are doing asas all the earners together can't even compare to Richie Ambition Is Evil: Very power-hungry and very evil. Anyone Can Die: Unexpectedly shot to death by his fiancee in a domestic dispute.

characters.name: Ralph "Ralphie" Cifaretto
characters.description: The Soprano crew's troublemaking top-earner. He is introduced in Season 3 when he rejoins the Jersey crew after an extended stay in Florida. Affably Evil:Zig-Zagged. He has a relatively lighthearted demeanor and is always cracking jokes, but he's frequently tone-deaf and can't read the room, so most people find him obnoxious. Alas, Poor Villain: A peculiar example of the grayness of the show. Despite being a despicable excuse for a human being most of the time, the tragic circumstances that surround his demise are meant to evoke some sympathy, given his son being in a coma and sets up hisHeel–Face Door-Slam(see below). Ambiguous Situation: It's never explicitly confirmed that he set the fire which killed Pie-Oh-My.David Chase has given conflicting answers, including a blunt"yes", whileJoe Pantoliano has said he played the scene as if Ralph was innocent. Anyone Can Die: His status as a big earner makes him less expendable than most in-story. When his demise comes, the when and the why are completely out of the blue.

characters.name: Carlo Gervasi
characters.description: Capo in theDiMeocrime family as of Season 4. Ascended Extra: Barely seen in the first few seasons, he becomes very important by Season 6. Berserk Button: Even insinuating Carlo might be gay makes him erupt with pure violence. He's homophobic even by the standards of the mafia. Beware the Quiet Ones: Initially a very soft-spoken background character with few lines, he reveals himself in Season 6 to be a very vicious individual with a high capacity for homophobic violence. He also becomes a major problem for Tony at the end of the series by (possibly) testifying against him. Broken Pedestal: He owes a lot to Tony, but disrespect and cynical commentary on the life tarnish Carlo's opinion of the man.

characters.name: Raymond "Ray" Curto
characters.description: A long-running capo in the family. Affably Evil: He's a soft-spoken, aging mobster who seems to get along with everyone, including (and especially) the Feds who he feeds information to over many seasons. Ambiguous Situation: Exactlywhenhe became an FBI informant is unknown beyond it happening before Season 3. He could have only turned over after being arrested at the brothel, but there's also the possibility that he was ratting before then and may have been a key in the bust up at said brothel. The lack of focus on Ray throughout the series combined with his abrupt death leaves this mystery unsolved. Beneath Notice: He seems to prefer it this way asit deflects attention from being an FBI informant. Beware the Quiet Ones: He's fairly low-key and mostly in the background, but he is the longest-running known rat during the course of the series.

characters.name: Vito Spatafore
characters.description: A rising member from the Cifaretto crew, nephew of Jackie and Richie Aprile, and a closeted homosexual. All Gays are Promiscuous:Downplayed. He does hook-up with a security guard before work on one occasion, but he's probably no more promiscuous than a lot of the straight guys in the mob who have goomahs and get action from girls at the Bing and such like. Alas, Poor Villain: Vito definitely isn't a good person, but he dies in such a brutal and undignified manner that it's hard not to feel bad for him. It doesn't help that he was killed merely for being gay rather than any of the actual crimes he committed in his career as a mobster. Ambiguously Bi: Although he's referred to as homosexual, he has two children, a wife, and more than one goomah. He's also said to have attempted to hook up with Adriana while Chris was hospitalized. The possibility of bisexuality never comes up, probably as it's very unlikely an ultra-macho and homophobic culture (where even going down on awomanis seen as evidence of homosexuality) as the mafia would have nuanced views on queerness. It is implied during Season 6 that he has lost any sexual interest in his wife and goomah, but it isn't made clear whether or not he has lost sexual interest in women generally or whether that's just a consequence of the difficult times he is going through. Ambiguous Situation: It's not exactly clear whether Vito was planning to murder Finn after taking him to the ball game. The episode strongly implies that Vito wants to ensure his silence in any way possible, but when Vito gets stood up, he still goes in to watch the game, implying that the game wasn'tjustan excuse to get Finn alone. We don't see Vito make any overt attempts to harm Finn thereafter, so it's possible Vito really was just going to take Finn aside and ask him to remain silent about what he saw.There are two examples of him interacting with Finn thereafter which could be considered mild threats or harassment. The first is when Tony is in hospi

characters.name: James "Jimmy" Altieri
characters.description: One of the original five captains and capo of the Altieri crew at the start of the series. Artifact Name: His crew seems to retain his name long after he is dead and outed as a rat. Ambiguous Situation: As sketchy as his behavior was, Jimmy, unlike every other notable rat in the series, is never explicitly shown cooperating with the FBI, nor do they discuss him or his fate other than to reassure Big Pussy that Jimmy's death has freed him of suspicion. His reaction to his impending death has also been interpreted a number of ways by fans, some of whom believehis despair after Silvio shows up was brought on more by knowing he was a dead man no matter what than any real admission of guilt. Boxed Crook: Implied to have turned state's witness after being arrested during an FBI raid on a pool hall he owns. Cigar Chomper: Almost never seen without one.

characters.name: Lorenzo "Larry Boy" Barese
characters.description: One of the original five captains and capo of the Barese crew at the start of the series. Affably Evil: Possibly the nicest and most soft-spoken out of any of the capos. Even his occasional ball-busting comes off as friendly and endearing rather than malicious. Bearer of Bad News: Breaks the news to all of the capos during his daughter's wedding in "The Legend of Tennessee Moltisanti" that the FBI is preparing to hand out federal indictments. This ends up ruining the wedding after all of the attending Mafiosi abruptly leave out of paranoia. Ironically, he is only one of threeDiMeoMafiosi to receive an indictment. Cigar Chomper: Frequently seen with one. Commuting on a Bus/Demoted to Extra: After he is sent to jail in the season 1 finale, he only appears from time to time, but maintains his captaincy throughout the series.

characters.name: Albert "Ally Boy" Barese
characters.description: Acting capo of the Barese crew. Bunny-Ears Lawyer: Despite his strange habit of repeating what his fellow mobsters are saying, Albert is actually a high earner within the family who successfully holds the Barese crew together while his cousin is away and is one of the more dangerous fighters in the card game robbery. Department of Redundancy Department: HisVerbal Ticof repeating other people's words, and this line which he says to Richie Aprile:(Referring to Larry): He's in no position to go into the unknown not knowing. The Echoer: It isn't for nothing that Paulie once referred to him as a "fucking parakeet". He does this to such a degree that, when Tonyuses Albert's very own tic against him, Albert just copies him right back. Even Evil Has Standards: While he despises Ralph like most of the other capos, he thinks it's messed up that Tony murdered Ralph just because Ralph killed a horse Tony was fond of.

characters.name: Gianluigi "Gigi" Cestone
characters.description: An enforcer in Junior's crew introduced in Season 2. Affably Evil: He can be polite and calm, but he has been shown to brutally murder other made men and wanted to (understandably) do so to Ralphie Cifaretto. Boring, but Practical: Lacks any of Ralph's flamboyancy, which makes him a more dependable captain and a forgettable character, this becomes gradually subverted as Tony begins to consider stripping Gigi of his captaincy as his boring methods don't bring enough money. Butt-Monkey: While an effective mobster, he finds himself constantly undermined byRalphwhen he takes over the Aprile crew, to say nothing of having what may be the most unceremonious death in the entire series. The Can Kicked Him: The guy suffers a fatal heart attack on the Bada Bing toilet, attending to nature’s call.

characters.name: Murphy "Murf" Lupo
characters.description: Philly Parisi's replacement as Capo of Junior's crew following the latter's murder. Authority in Name Only: He is a Capo on paper but only has two soldiers (another old guy and Bobby) under his command and is unable to make many decisions due to how much influence Junior is allowed to have over their crew. Dangerous Senior Driver: Inverted. Junior mocks him for driving "like an old woman". Dork in a Sweater: The status of Capo often comes with fancy suits but Murf is a physically and mentally weak old guy whose fanciest attire is a sweater. Remember the New Guy?: He is a senior soldier in Junior’s crew but is never even mentioned in season one.

characters.name: Carmine Lupertazzi Sr.
characters.description: Longtime don of the Lupertazzi crime family. Affably Evil: Despite being utterly ruthless in his business dealings, Carmine is nonetheless a doting father to his son, Little Carmine, and prefers to resolve tensions with the Sopranos through diplomacy rather than conflict. He is very rarely, if ever, shown to lose his temper with anyone. Amazingly Embarrassing Parents: Asks his middle-aged son Carmine Jr. if he's put his sunblock on, in front of Johnny Sack. Big Bad: Of Season 4. The season's biggest source of conflict centers around his organization's efforts to run roughshod over theDiMeocrime family either under his orders or with his consent. Towards the end of the season, the tensions between himself and Tony threaten to boil over into an all-outMob War. Blank Stare: When Johnny Sack repeats Ralph's joke to him.

characters.name: "Little" Carmine Lupertazzi Jr.
characters.description: Carmine Lupertazzi's son and heir apparent. Affably Evil: Arguably one of the nicest guys in the show. He is rarely seen engaging in the usual criminal activities of the mob (ordering hits, screwing people over, etc) and is usually doing more benign things like making movies. The most annoyed or angry he's ever seen to be is perhaps when his boat gets wrecked. Always Someone Better: Carmine is a wealthy Mafia prince, but he realizes that he's just a small fry compared to Hollywood elite. Big Bad Wannabe: He tries to take over as the boss of his father's crime family. Aside from not being competent enough for the role, he also does not have the stomach for violence. This actually works in his favor, since staying away from the Mafia means he’s one of the few characters for whom the series ends on a high note for. Contrasting Replacement Character: He is this to Jackie Jr, as he is introduced in Season 4 long after Jackie Jr. is killed. Both of them had fathers who were powerful criminal mob bosses who share their name, both aren't really too bright and neither one of them get any respect from some of their peers. But their fates turn out to be otherwise. Jackie was a young man trying to fast-track into the criminal life dropping out of school, not fully knowing the extent of the mob life and ends up getting killed after the card game stunt left Sunshine and some of his own crew dead. Carmine was an older man, meaning he was fully aware of how the mob life is and knowing it too well that it's not worth it at the end of the day, giving the role of the boss to Johnny Sack and instead focuses on his own civilian life, and whenever he is involved in mob conflict, he tends to be a neutral party. Carmine also genuinely loved his wife, while Jackie kept cheating on Meadow.

characters.name: John "Johnny Sack" Sacrimoni
characters.description: Underboss of the Lupertazzi crime family. A longtime friend of Tony Soprano, his main role in the series is as New York's liaison with the mob in New Jersey. He eventually moves to N.J. himself. Affably Evil: Whilst not exactly nice, he is usually calm and rational. As long as you are not insulting his wife. Alas, Poor Villain:He's given a rare empathetic death, dying after a long illness and surrounded by his anguished family, underscoring that a broken mobster is still a human being. In-universe, even the gangsters who are disappointed in him breaking the Omertà are saddened by his passing and honor his memory. All for Nothing: Johnny spent his life at the top of the mafia hierarchy and wins a mob war to become boss of New York, yet only a few years later, he's in prison and has almost all of his earnings seized.On top of that, he breaks the Omertà in his trial (and therefore ruining his reputation) for the sake of reducing his sentence only to die long before he could even serve it. Ascended Extra: In the first couple of seasons he appears rarely (usually at gatherings). He gets more screentime starting in season three (when he moves to New Jersey) and becomes a key character from season four onwards.

characters.name: Phillip "Phil" Leotardo
characters.description: A hot-headed capo in the Lupertazzi family, released from prison in Season 5. He ends up in a leadership position, causing a great deal of conflict in the process. Aesop Amnesia: Shortly after Tony makes an impassioned plea for peace to him following a near-death experience, Phil begins contemplating thoughts of retirement as well as adopting a more pacifist approach to life in general. However, his old ruthless, bloodthirsty personality resurfaces after his protégé, Gerry Torciano, is murdered by "Doc" Santoro and he blames this turn of events on his own "weakness". Arch-Enemy: Quickly becomes Tony's most persistent and vicious foe,especially once he finally guns for Tony himself and ends up having Bobby killed. Putting Silvio in a comacements how far Phil is willing to take his grudge, waging and dragging on a conflict in which even the Lupertazzi leadership concludes that the only solution isPhil's death. Armored Closet Gay: It’s heavily implied that Phil’s extreme hatred of homosexuality is self-loathing due to him having had sex with men in prison. When rumors about Vito’s sexuality surface, Phil immediately becomes obsessed with them and turns almost every conversation with Tony into an opportunity to throw slurs and death threats Vito’s way.When Vito is ambushed in a motel room by Phil’s men lying in wait, Phil literally comes out of a closet to greet him, and is seen gripping the bed in a sexually suggestive manner while his men beat Vito to death.Series creatorDavid Chaseconfirms Phil did have sex with men in prison on theTalking Sopranospodcast. Ascended Extra: After he is mentioned on TV, he mostly shows up in the background at the beginning of Season 5, and then plays only a minor role midway through. It isn't until Billy is killed that he is shot-gunned into being the main antagonist.

characters.name: Butch "Butchie"DeConcini
characters.description: Phil's right-hand man after Gerry Torciano gets "retired". Blood Knight: Even when Phil is willing to cease hostilities, Butchie continues to antagonize Tony further. Boisterous Weakling: At first he talks big about decapitating the New Jersey mob and how Tony doesn't have any balls to just come in and stab someone with an icepick. Then Tony drive to New York to beat Coco and all Butchie can do is sit down and makes himself small. As the war goes on he realized they bit more than they could chew. The Consigliere: Phil's. Surprisingly, he's more confrontational and bloodthirsty than his boss, until Tony beats Coco in front of Butchie and threatens him to stay seated at gunpoint. After that Butchie is more eager to sue peaceful arrangements when the battle is uncertain. Dirty Coward: For all his talk he folds fast under immediate threat of violence.

characters.name: Albert "Albie" Cianflone
characters.description: A trusted associate of Phil Leotardo's since the 1980s. Becomes Phil's consigliere after his ascendancy to acting boss. Co-Dragons: With Butchie, to Phil. Albie overall is the more reasonable of the two. The Consigliere: Shares this position with Butchie, though in practice Albie mostly just ends up going along with whatever Phil wants to do. He briefly protests Phil's plan towipe out the leadership in Jerseybut falls in line with little effort. Fat Bastard: Downplayed as he's one of the more pleasant and reasonable guys in the Lupertazzi family, but he's quite overweight and is a close supporter ofPhil Leotardo. Satellite Character: Only ever shown accompanying other members of the Lupertazzi crew and receives little independent characterization.

characters.name: Rusty Millio
characters.description: A captain in the Lupertazzi family who advises Carmine Jr. during his war with Johnny Sack. Awful Wedded Life: We don't see much of it, but his final scene hints that he barely tolerates his wife. Boom, Headshot!:The way he's retired. Celebrity Paradox: Frankie Valli is an acquaintance of Tony's and has to be contacted by Silvio after a casino manager wants a favor returned. El Spanish "-o": His attemps at Italian are terrible.Move-ah el automobile-eh!

characters.name: Angelo Garepe
characters.description: Former consigliere of Carmine Lupertazzi. Released from prison at the beginning of Season 5 as one of the "Class of '04", and seeks to retire. Affably Evil: Hardly even counts as "evil" anymore; even as he's drawn back into the Lupertazzi syndicate, he remains fairly benign, outside of conspiring to have Joey Peeps murdered. Ain't Too Proud to Beg: Pleads with Phil just before he is shot. Anti-Villain: The fella just wanted a civilian life after prison, shame Tony Soprano forgot the memo and proposes Angelo to be a part of a"triunva thing" to share power in New York. The Consigliere: To Carmine Lupertazzi, and later to his son, though Little Carmine generally favors Rusty Millio's advice over Angelo's.

characters.name: William "Billy" Leotardo
characters.description: The younger brother of Phil Leotardo. The Apprentice: Phil grooms him into becoming an enforcer and a made man. The Baby of the Bunch: Subverted.
