He is NOT a kid, being 44 when he died. However, many characters tend to call him 'kid' or 'boy', as if he's a young new mafioso. EvenChristopher, who is at least a decade younger than Billy, called him a kid at one point. The Brute: He's noticably bulky and serves as John's enforcer alongside Joey Peeps. This is best seen when he manages to take down Lorraine Calluzzo's musclebound boyfriend Jason and beat up Angelo before Phil killed him. Cynicism Catalyst: While Billy was alive, Phil was a restrainable soldier, almost amiable by Phil's own standards. After Billy dies, Phil never gets over it and is helplessly embittered, which eventually drives him to stop compromising and to break the status quo.

characters.name: Joey "Peeps" Peparelli
characters.description: Protégé of Johnny Sack. Accidental Misnaming: His headstone is carved with his nickname "Peeps", to general dismay, in particularJohnny's. Affably Evil: Aside from beating and intimidating Lorraine and murdering Jason, he's a very genial guy. The Apprentice: For Johnny Sack. Phil more directly mentors him as an enforcer, however. Ascended Extra: To an extent. He was first seen in two Season 4 episodes as an aide-de-camp to Johnny Sack and Carmine Lupertazzi. His death in Season 5 is one of the major plot points of the season.

characters.name: James "Jimmy" Petrille
characters.description: Johnny Sack's right-hand man. Affably Evil: Tony mentions that he is a "sweet old guy". The Consigliere: Johnny's. Diabolus ex Machina: He functions as a character version. We learn basically nothing about him and he only appears onscreen for a few minutes total, until it's randomly revealed he was an FBI informant all along and gets Johnny Sack arrested, putting the much more psychotic Phil into the leadership of the Lupertazzi family. Jimmy's role fulfilled, he completely disappears from the story afterwards. Minor Major Character: Despite being Johnny's consigliere, he has minimal weight in the story until he rats on John and disappears from the narrative.

characters.name: Faustino "Doc" Santoro
characters.description: The much-reviled predecessor to Phil Leotardo as head of the Lupertazzi family. 0% Approval Rating: Despite having enough pull to become boss, a good chunk of the Lupertazzi's captains can't stand him. Once he becomes boss, he gets whacked very quickly by Butch and other members of the family by Phil's orders. He also makes himself incredibly unpopular with the Lupertazzis' Jersey partners by using Silvio to lure Gerry into a trap. Asshole Victim: The guy was such a prick that even his fellow mobsters hated his guts. It's safe to say no one really blamed Phil for having him killed. Contempt Crossfire: Phil obviously hates Doc for whacking his personally handpicked successor, the other Lupertazzi captains already have a low opinion of Doc due to his slimy personality, and he also earns the ire of theDiMeofamily members due to using Silvio as a distraction for Gerry's whacking (Silvio was so close that Gerry's blood splattered on his face and he was deafened by the gunshot). Dude, Where's My Respect?: Severely offends Phil Leotardo by literally eating the food off his plate, and this after Doc had Gerry whacked.

characters.name: Gerry "The Hairdo" Torciano
characters.description: Phil's second and would-be successor. Affably Evil: Seems to keep Phil's unending rage in check, to a degree. Phil really starts to go downhill after Gerry is killed. Blue Oni: A restraining counterbalance of Phil's red. Characterization Marches On: He's a blond in Season 6A. In Season 6B, he has black hair and a different haircut, very confusing changes that nobody points out, despite Gerry being known as "the hairdo". Cruel and Unusual Death: Gets shot multiple times by a hitman, but instead of dying instantly he's shown reacting in pain to each shot before falling off his chair, then is shown futilely trying to crawl away from his killer in a crippled and visibly agonized state before being finished off.

characters.name: Dominic "Fat Dom" Gamiello
characters.description: A heavy subordinate of Phil Leotardo. Accidental Murder: Well, at least on Sil's part. Silvio initiates a confrontation by hitting Dom in the head with a handheld vacuum, and then prompts Carlo to "hit him". However Sil screams "No!" when Carlo reaches for a kitchen knife, apparently having intended to simply beat Dom up to teach him a lesson. When Carlo sticks the knife in Dom's chest, there's no going back for either of them. Asshole Victim: He's in fact killed for being an asshole, pushing Carlo and Silvio with insulting jokes, inside their own headquarters. Blame Game: When Tony shows up and sees Dom's corpse, Silvio starts to explain what happened. Carlo (who has killed Dom with four stabs) sheepishly pins it on Silvio, who technically did initiate the fatal confrontation.Sivlio: Fat Dom Gamiello came over, just to break balls [...] Carlo...Carlo:Sil hit him first. Bloody Hilarious: His death is really something tobehold. TheBlack Comedyextends to the aftermath, with Carlo and Silvio passing the time until the night playing cards and eating something, like in a picnic... with Dom's corpse lying in another table a few feet away from them!

characters.name: Salvatore "Coco" Cogliano
characters.description: A subordinate of Phil and restaurant owner. Alcohol-Induced Idiocy: Meadow mentions he reeked of Sambuca when he harassed her. Curb-Stomp Battle: Tony gives him a literal one for harassing Meadow. Dirty Old Man: He sexually harasses Meadow in front of her date by making several lewd comments. This leads to a very literalCurb-Stomp Battledelivered by Tony. Facial Horror: It's probably for the best that the aftermath of his injury wasn't shown.

characters.name: Sal Iacuzzo
characters.description: Politically Incorrect Villain: While being given due to him being a made man, he takes a particular disgust when spotting Vito dancing with a man in the gay bar. Small Role, Big Impact: He doesn't appear anymore past his one scene, but in that scene, he spotted Vito in the gay bar he was extorting money from, leading to both the Soprano and Lupertazzi Crews finding out about Vito's homosexuality, and all the things that happened after that. Unwitting Instigator of Doom: Him informing his cousin about Vito led toVito getting outed, him fleeing New Jersey, his subsequent death after he returned as well as the tension between the crews becoming even higher after the news reached Phil's ears. What Happened to the Mouse?: It's unknown what happened to him after theMob Warbetween the Lupertazzis and the Sopranos.

characters.name: Emil Kolar
characters.description: Small Role, Big Impact: He has the "honor" of being Chris's first victim, eventually hardening him into a ruthless mafioso. Too Dumb to Live: He goes to meet Chris, a mobster from a rival gang,alone. Chris ends up killing him with no witnesses. Wrong Genre Savvy: Emil believed that he is in a fiction with a reasonable gangster code where they don'tShoot the Messenger, and thereby went to meet with him all alone. Chris proves him fatally wrong.

characters.name: Lorraine Calluzzo
characters.description: A rare female loan shark known as "Lady Shylock" and associate of the Lupertazzi crime syndicate. Ain't Too Proud to Beg: Begs for her life by offering to blow the Leotardo brothers. It turns out to be a mock execution, however. Phil makes fun of the situation andwarns herthat "Next time there won't be a next time". Asshole Victim: Downplayed, the audience is informed she was a very trigger-happyLoan Shark, but very little of that is shown. Butt-Monkey: Her screen time is largely spent being humiliated by the Leotardos. Fan Disservice: Has a nice body. She is running away naked before the Leotardo brothers kill her.

characters.name: Matush Giamona
characters.description: A Persian drug dealer who frequents Adriana's club, the Crazy Horse. Chekhov's Gunman: His efforts to sell drugs in the Crazy Horse are seemingly just a one-episode side plot to further Jackie Jr.'s story arc. However, he reappears two seasons later, now having solid roots for his operation in Crazy Horse, and ends up killing a guy in Adriana's office. This, in turn, leads toAdriana's death when she tries to cover it up. Karma Houdini: Sure, he gets his ass kicked for dealing drugs at one point, but in the larger picture, he is extremely lucky. First, he acts as the getaway driver forJackie Jr.when he and some friends rob Eugene's card game. When shots ring out, Giamona drives off, leaving his buddies behind, and everyone iseventually killed but him. Then a few seasons later, hemurders someone in the back of Adriana's club, the FBI targetsher thanks to her connection to Christopher, and she is eventually killed for being an informant; meanwhile, Matush literally gets away with murder and faces no repercussions from the FBI or Christopher.However, it should be noted that when Adriana recounts the details of the incident at the club, the FBI agents become visibly intrigued by Adriana relating Matush's "strong religious beliefs", as well as the fact that he regularly sends money back to Pakistan, and that Matush's brother runs a "prep school" of some type. And towards the end of the episode, even when by all appearances their gambit to use Adriana to make Christopher flip has failed utterly, the agents are still fixated on the Nieves murder by Matush and resolve to take over the investigation from the Long Branch police department, as it may be terrorist-related. So with all that, it is not unreasonable to presume that the FBI will eventually nail Giamona, ultimately making this a case ofKarma Houdini Warranty. Months later, Agent Harris brings up Matush in a conversation about possible terrorist activity with Christopher in "Join The Club", revealing his last name "Gi

characters.name: Warren Feldman
characters.description: A convict and former oncologist who befriends the ailing Johnny Sack late in the series. Almighty Janitor: He's an orderly who spent decades as a doctor, specializing in oncology, and still knows his stuff, able to give advice on the best form of treatment. The main doctor on the ward even has to warn him to stop giving medical advice and undermining his authority. The Atoner: It's not given much focus but his conversation with John implies he's this. Cool Old Guy: He's a pretty charismatic individual and his conversations with Johnny seem to be the closest thing the latter gets to a respite in his dying days. Drugs Are Bad: He had a nasty cocaine habit and went on a killing spree in drug-induced haze, for which he was arrested and convicted. After kicking the habit in prison, he became a much more affable person.

characters.name: Salvatore "Mustang Sally" Intile
characters.description: A small-time thug with an infamous temper. He is whacked by Bobby Baccalieri, Senior when he goes too far and puts Vito Spatafore's brother in the hospital. Asshole Victim: Normally having your brains splattered across a kitchen ceiling is a horrible fate, but Mustang Sally 100% deserved it. Ax-Crazy: Threw a vendor off a balcony at Yankee Stadium for putting too many onions on his hotdog. He also beats a complete stranger into a coma because his girlfriend asked the guy for a car ride. Berserk Button: He's extremely jealous and any indication that someone is trying to get close to his girlfriend, even just talking to her in his presence, will send him into a violent rage. Boom, Headshot!: How he dies.

characters.name: "Black" Jack Massarone
characters.description: Owner of Massarone Construction. Baddie Flattery: This is what dooms him. He tells Tony that he has lost weight, which by Season 5 is something that flies in the face of everyone with eyes. Tony later picks up on this smarminess as the proof he needs to murder Massarone. Bad Liar: Massarone is extremely shifty and anxious in his later appearances with Tony. This serves to indicate his position as a mole for the FBI, but Tony fails to pick up any signs in their interactions, and only later realizes he was given an insincere compliment. The Con: Victim of a semi-classic protection racket; goes to Tony for protection against a picket organized by Tony. Due to the Dead: A golf club cover is stuffed in his mouth when he is retired, in order to deliver a message about rats and snitching.

characters.name: Jesus Rossi
characters.description: Dr. Melfi's rapist who gets free on a technicality, leading to her debating whether she should sic Tony on him or not. Antagonist Title: The titularEmployee of the Month. Employee of the Month: A particularly disturbing example that highlights how easily he is able to blend in. From Nobody to Nightmare: A lowly fast food employee who ends up being one of the vilest, most repugnant characters in the series. Hate Sink: Has no character beyond being a violent rapist. The fact that he never faces any consequences for his actions doesn't help either.

characters.name: Adriana La Cerva
characters.description: Christopher Moltisanti's girlfriend, and later fiancee. Ascended Extra: Quite literally, in the very first episode she appears for a few seconds as a hostess at a restaurant before getting a name in episode 2 and finally getting storylines in the seasons after that. Babies Make Everything Better: She's a firm believer in this, convinced that if she could have children, her and Chris's relationship would clear up. The fact that she can't have themmakes it all the more tragic. Brainless Beauty: She's noted on numerous occasions to be extremely attractive, but she's not intelligent at all, and makes a lot of stupid decisions which lead up to her death . Most notable of these is her devotion to a violent sociopath like Christopher, to the point where multiple characters wonder why she sticks with him. Tony is able to easily trick her into a death trap due to her devotion to Christopher. Break the Cutie: While some of this may cross over withToo Dumb to Live, Adriana starts the series as just a dim, sweet girl who wants to have children with Christopher. As time goes on, however, things just keep getting worse for her, and she gets thoroughly broken once she becomes an informant for the FBI. Chris spirals further into drug addiction, it's revealed that she's infertile, Chris becomes increasingly physically violent towards her, the FBI aggressively pressures her into giving up more and more information, and once she confides in Chris and tries to convince him to run away with her, he chooses the family over her and sells her out to Tony, who has her killed.

characters.name: Kelli Lombardo-Moltisanti
characters.description: Chris' girlfriend and eventual wife in Season 6. Contrasting Replacement Character: To Adriana. Ade was outspoken, aggressive, independent, and willing to stand up to Christopher; Kelli is more reserved, less confident, and displays no ambition beyond supporting Chris as his stay-at-home wife. Ade was barren, but loved by Chris in the midst of a destructive relationship that broke him and doomed her; Kelli gives Chris a family, but they were wed more due to caprice and obligation on his part than love, and whatever they share doesn't sufficiently motivate Christopher to stop indulging hiseventually fataldrug habit. Narratively, Ade was at the heart of a significant storyline and had some agency beyond "Christopher's girlfriend", while Kelli never grows beyond aSatellite Love Interest. Foreshadowing: Silvio warned Christopher that marrying Adriana, whom he loved but who struggled to conceive, would make him happier in the fullness of time than the contrivance of a family with "some twat." While that's an unfair appraisal of Kelli'scharacter, Christopher never truly gets over Adriana and rushes into a hollow marriage with Kelli, whom he unintentionally knocked up. Fourth-Date Marriage: Heavily implied. Although we never find out how long they've been together, it cannot have been for more than a few months. Christopher proposes to Kelli the verysceneshe's introduced in, and quickly regrets his choice after the shotgun ceremony when he discovers he doesn't really love her (although Kelli doesn't notice). Happily Married: Only on Kelli's side as she seems quite content in her marriage to Christopher and, outside of his cheating, doesn't suffer from theDomestic Abusethat he put Adriana through. Christopher, however, sees this as anAwful Wedded Lifeas he can't find it in him to feel real love for Kelli and only married her because he got her pregnant.

characters.name: Tracee
characters.description: A stripper at the Bada Bing and Ralph Cifaretto's girlfriend. Abusive Parents: She burned her young son with cigarettes and the kid was taken by social services.She implies this was due to her being on the unkind end of this trope, too. Bullying a Dragon: She sees fit to insult and smack Ralph, a dangerous gangster. It doesn't end well. Buxom Beauty Standard: Tony notes that, unlike most strippers at the Bing, she has no need for breast implants. Cruel and Unusual Death: Ralph beats her to death in the parking lot of the Bing, while she's pregnant with Ralph's child, no less,who would contest that point later.

characters.name: Rosalie Aprile
characters.description: Wife of the late Jackie Aprile Sr. A good friend of Carmela's; they seem to have a standing lunch date at Vesuvio, and she shows up whenever Carmela or her family is in trouble. Carm often turns to her for advice. Affably Evil: The immorality of marrying a mob boss aside, Rosalie is usually quite pleasant and a very good friend to Carmela. The Artifact:Justified. She is the wife of Jackie Sr, who dies in the fourth episode, and could have easily been written out and never seen or mentioned again. However, she is established as the best friend of Carmela towards the end of the first season and maintains value as a character just on that basis. This is to say nothing of her brother-in-law Richie and son Jackie Jr showing up later, and her relationship with Ralphie. Ascended Extra: She is something of aDownplayedexample. Her first appearance is as the wife of the dying boss Jackie Sr several episodes into the series. She doesn't come into the picture again until the end of the first season, in which she plays a crucial part in ending the infatuation between Carmela and Father Phil. From then on she makes regular appearances to the point of probably being the most prominent of the mob spouses besides Carmela and Adriana. Brutal Honesty: Doesn't mince words when doling out needed advice to Carmela about sensitive matters, like troubles with Tony and AJ, not to mention Carm's extramarital romantic entanglements.

characters.name: Ginny Sacrimoni
characters.description: Big Beautiful Woman: She's the butt of jokes for most of the mob guys, but John describes her as "Rubenesque" and she is naturally attractive. Big Girl: This puts her at the center of many jokes. Break the Cutie: It's hard not to feel sorry for Ginny Sack by the end of the series. Generation Xerox: Her daughter Allegra has a similar figure. Averted with Catherine who is very thin. Happily Married: She enjoys a good marriage with Johnny, who stays faithful to his wife, unlike all the other mobsters (except Bobby Baccala).

characters.name: Patty Leotardo
characters.description: Phil Leotardo's harridan of a wife. Happily Married: Perhaps her only redeeming quality as a human being is her genuine love for her family. She truly does love Phil and is horrified when he is shot in front of her, before her chief concern is for her infant grandchildren. Heteronormative Crusader:When Vito is outed as gay, Patty declares him immoral on religious grounds and calls his homosexuality an unforgivable sin. In comparison, Phil's anger against Vito seems more based on how he is his cousin-in-law and being worried about how having a "fanook" in the family is going to reflect on him.The crowning example is perhaps when Patty invites a right-wing Protestant reverend who claims to be an expert in "curing" homosexuality to do a talk at her church group, despite considering herself a proper Catholic. When Vito is outed as gay, Patty declares him immoral on religious grounds and calls his homosexuality an unforgivable sin. In comparison, Phil's anger against Vito seems more based on how he is his cousin-in-law and being worried about how having a "fanook" in the family is going to reflect on him. The crowning example is perhaps when Patty invites a right-wing Protestant reverend who claims to be an expert in "curing" homosexuality to do a talk at her church group, despite considering herself a proper Catholic.

characters.name: Karen Baccalieri
characters.description: Bobby Baccalieri's wife. A Death in the Limelight/Satellite Character: Her character is introduced only to be killed a few episodes later. Happily Married: Implied, despite her little screen time showing mild discussions with Bobby.

characters.name: Nicole Lupertazzi
characters.description: Little Carmine's wife. There's a great case to be made that she, like her husband, is theonly sane personon this page. Foil: Much like Little Carmine becomes one to Tony, she is one to Carmela. Where the wealth is evidently enough to keep Carmela there in the mob lifestyle, Nicole helped her husband come to the conclusion that it ultimately was not worth it. Happily Married: After court-ordered therapy after an unspecified "thing." Evidently it worked extraordinarily well, with her notably begging Carmine to quit because she didn't want to be "the wealthiest widow on Long Island." Karmic Jackpot: Much like her husband. Pulling Carmine away from civil war in New York results in her receiving one of the extraordinarily rare happy endings of the show... and earns the distinction of "Only mob wife that's (probably) not a widow." Morality Chain: She is the one pulling Carmine away from the mafia power plays. Her reluctance to become "the wealthiest widow on Long Island" inspired Carmine to step back from his ambition of becoming boss and instead choose to live a happy life with his family.

characters.name: Gabriella Dante
characters.description: Casting Gag: She's played by Silvio's actor's real life wife. Happily Married: She and Silvio have a good relationship, despite his infidelity. I Was Quite a Looker: According to Tony. Lady Macbeth: A very mild form. When Tonyis in the hospital after being shot by Junior, she encourages Sil to consider taking over after Tony is gone. That said, she never advises him to hurry the process along—merely to throw his hat into the ring when theSuccession Crisishits. Obnoxious Entitled Housewife: After she and the other mob wives attend a church event where the speaker speaks negatively of the mafia, she throws a fit to Father Intintola and threatens that their group will cut off their financial support to the parish.

characters.name: Angie Bonpensiero
characters.description: Sal "Big Pussy" Bonpensiero's wife. The Artifact: She is the wife of a character whodies in the second season, but stays around for pretty much the rest of the series in a minor supporting role. Character Development: From a neurotic and dependent mess to ano-nonsense mob associateputting money on the street. The other mob wives are disquieted that she's becomeOne of the Guys. Domestic Abuse: Her marriage is not a happy one. Fallen-on-Hard-Times Job: Works in a supermarket to make ends meet after Pussy gets retired. This reinforces Carmela's anxiety about what would happen to her with Tony gone. Tony later takes pity on her and gives her a job at her husband's car shop, where she becomes quite a successful manager.

characters.name: Marie Spatafore
characters.description: Vito's wife and cousin of Phil Leotardo. Friendly Enemy: Indirectly, as she doesn't know that Phil is an enemy. She's a friend of Phil's wife (and a relative of Phil himself) and is on very good terms with the Leotardos, but to Phil this is irrelevant. Horrible Judge of Character: She honestly believes thatPhilis a trustworthy man and partly implores Vito to come back home because she believed him about sending Vito to psychiatric care. Phil rewards it by abandoning her family. Innocent Means Naïve: Has nothing to do with the mafia or its members beyond being married to one, and likewise is totally clueless about how forgiving they would be of Vito's homosexuality, their involvement in his death, or their willingness to financially provide for her after the fact. Real-Life Relative: Played by Elizabeth Bracco, real-life sister of Lorraine Bracco (Dr. Melfi).

characters.name: Tina Francesco
characters.description: A former stripper at Bada Bing! and later sweetheart to "Little" Paulie Gualtieri. Has a Type/All Girls Want Bad Boys: She dates "Mustang" Sally Intile and later "Little Paulie" Gualtieri, and shamelessly flirts with Chris, all men with ties to the Mafia. Uncertain Doom: When Adriana gets wise to her sexual chemistry with Chris, she exposes a financial scam Tina's involved in to her FBI handler. Tina's fate isn't elaborated upon, but that's the last we see of her. With Friends Like These...: Adriana's prospective maid of honor, with blatant designs on the groom. It's a sad commentary on Adriana's social life that she considers Tina her best friend.

characters.name: Violet Lupertazzi
characters.description: The wife of Carmine Lupertazzi Sr. The Faceless: She is mentioned on multiple occasions but almost never seen. The only reason for the word 'almost' is because there is a scene in which Carmine Sr is at a party and an elderly woman who could plausibly be his wife is sitting near him. Even if she is indeed Violet Lupertazzi, her face isn't seen. Happily Married: Even if it's in dream form, Carmine Sr talks about how much he loved his wife and how much he misses her. There aren't many indications of Carmine Sr having or being interested in goomahs.

characters.name: Irina Peltsin
characters.description: Tony's Russian goomah. Alcohol-Induced Idiocy: After Tony leaves her she becomes a catastrophic drunk dialler. Brainless Beauty: Tony finds her too childlike and simple. Bungled Suicide: A mix of pills and vodka, after Tony ends the relationship. Daddy Issues: As a result of her alcoholic father, who died at 55.

characters.name: Gloria Trillo
characters.description: A patient of Dr. Melfi who starts a turbulent affair with Tony. Bullying a Dragon: Trying to force Tony Soprano's hand by being aPsycho Ex-Girlfriend? Bad idea, Gloria. He can easily outgun you in the unsavory department. She invokes it more deliberately once she realizes Tony doesn't want her back, trying to provoke Tony into killing her. Bus Crash: She'sDriven to Suicideat some point offscreen. Mentioned in passing. Cute and Psycho: Tries to a pull aFatal Attractionmove on Tony, but Patsy Parisidiscourages her. Death Is Dramatic: She wants it to be. Gloria seduces and then angers Tony in the hopes that he will fulfill this wish. Tony throws cold water on this by having Patsy Parisi intimidate her with a very blunt description of how Tony will just have her unceremoniously murdered if she continues down this path. She later hangs herself from a chandelier, though the show itself manages to avert this trope in that instance as well by keeping it off-screen.

characters.name: Valentina La Paz
characters.description: Ralph's, and later Tony's goomah. Facial Horror: She's badly burned in a domestic accident. Tony was already planning on leaving her and is quite frustrated that it's now impossible not to look like he's dumping her over her looks. Femme Fatalons: Has absurdly long and ornate nails.Carmela discovering onepushes her to play a rather more serious prank of her own on Tony. Foe Cooties: Tony has his qualms at first since she's Ralph's comare, but loses them when he discoversshe and Ralphie don't really have sex, as such.Tony:He could technically not have penisary contact with her Volvo. The Mistress: Ralph's and then Tony's.

characters.name: Fran Felstein
characters.description: Johnny Boy Soprano's old goomah, who befriends Tony. Abhorrent Admirer: She ultimately becomes one for Tony. She'spast her prime, and she had a role in his issues with both Johnny Boy andLivia. Thecringeworthyreenactment of"Happy Birthday Mr. President"didn't help either. Gold Digger: Was this for Johnny Boy, and attempts to latch onto his son for a similar relationship. History with Celebrity: She had a fling withJohn F. Kennedy. I Can't Hear You: She frequently misses what Tony is saying because she's slightly deaf. By her own admission, she's too vain to wear a hearing aid.

characters.name: Julianna Skiff
characters.description: A Jewish real estate saleswoman who has an affair with Christopher and a near-affair with Tony. The Alcoholic: Drug addiction. Brainy Brunette: She's rather smart and cultured, especially when compared to the other women in Tony's life. The Danza: She shares her first name with her actress. Hello, Attorney!: Real estate broker. Incidentally, Julianna Margulies is the trope image.

characters.name: Sonya Aragon
characters.description: A Las Vegas based student who's paying for her degree with a side career in stripping. Was Chris's squeeze, then has a brief fling with Tony. Comforting the Widow: Tony's excuse for visiting her. Erudite Stoner: Mellow and thoughtful, at least by the standards Tony is used to. She helps him process his feelings aboutChris's deaththrough a peyote trip. Functional Addict: Does a lot of drugs, but aside from the stereotypical emotional detachment of a stoner she otherwise seems to have her head screwed on straight. Has a Type: Aside from being the very last of Tony's affairs with olive-skinned, statuesque, dark-haired women, she herself finds East Coast gangsters irresistible, mostly becausethey're so different to what's available on campus.

characters.name: Giuseppina Bruno
characters.description: Dickie Moltisanti's goomah. Before then she wasAldo Moltisanti's wife from Italy and Dickie's step-mother. Affectionate Gesture to the Nose:Just before she nervously admits to sleeping with Harold, Dickie tries to calm her down, by kissing her all over the face, the first two on the nose.Earlier in the movie, when they are in the house he buys her, and engaging in puppy love normally shown between much younger couples, he taps her on the nose at one point. Just before she nervously admits to sleeping with Harold, Dickie tries to calm her down, by kissing her all over the face, the first two on the nose. Earlier in the movie, when they are in the house he buys her, and engaging in puppy love normally shown between much younger couples, he taps her on the nose at one point. Asshole Victim: Awful as her murder is, she doesn't engender a lot of sympathy after having cheated on Dickie with his enemy and wanting Harold to murder him over something as petty and trivial as him being cautious about the particulars of buying her a hair salon, after havingalready bought her a houseand her having been his well taken care of goomah for years by that point. And this after he murdered his own father in part to protect her fromhim.

characters.name: Dwight Harris
characters.description: A senior FBI agent assigned to Tony's investigation. Anti-Hero: Of theKnight in Sour Armorvariant. He possesses a cold and humorless demeanor, but he is a good guy who is doing his job to maintain the peace. He also helps Tony assassinate a rival mob boss by leaking crucial information about Phil's whereabouts. Awful Wedded Life: Near the end of the series, he's seen arguing over the phone with his wife, who clearly doesn't like that he'sMarried to the Job, and it's obvious that this isn't their first such argument. Harris is later shown having an affair with another FBI agent. Dirty Cop: His opposition to LCN is never in question, but he's cordial with the mobsters on a personal level and possesses an "ends justify the means" type of mindset. In the end, he's a party tothe murder of a mob boss. Enemy Mine: His final scene in the series is him celebratingthe death of Phil Leotardo, which he helped arrange with Tony.

characters.name: Frank Cubitoso
characters.description: An FBI director in charge of investigations into the Soprano family. Big Good: Technically, what with being the highest ranking FBI agent seen on the show. FBI Agent: He's the chief of the FBI's New Jersey division. Good Is Not Nice: Although mostly a calm, soft-spoken man, he scares the relatively innocent (by the standards of this show) Adriana into becoming an informer with the threat of a very long prison sentence for drug dealing, so much that she vomits all over him. In her final episode he berates and threatens her for not giving him useful info (although his reason is justified, as Adriana has become complicit in a murder at the Crazy Horse which she had tried to hide from both the FBI and Christopher). Jerkass Has a Point: Telling Adriana that if she's imprisoned for drug trafficking she's likely to be targeted by Tony for having brought an FBI agent to his house is tantamount to threatening her into cooperating, but it's unfortunately the hard truth of the matterand exactly what happens when Tony eventually does find out she flipped.

characters.name: Robyn Sanservino
characters.description: An FBI agent who notably serves as handler to Adriana La Cerva. Being Personal Isn't Professional: She lies about having children when Adriana picks her brain on the topic, but she does betray a little of her private life when she relates her reasons for joining the FBI. Butt-Monkey: She handles Federal witnesses Adriana La Cerva, Eugene Pontecorvo, and Ray Curto.Adriana is murdered, Eugene commits suicide, and Ray dies of an aneurysmin Robyn's car. Failure Hero: She functions as the handler for three mob informants, but her success rate is worse than nothing. All three of her informants end up dying without giving up anything useful, one of whom diesmid-conversationwith her. Freudian Excuse: She tells Adriana that the reason she became an FBI agent is because her sister was rendered a paraplegic by her (the sister's) boyfriend,because he was trying to open a coconut by shooting at it and it ricocheted at her. It was then she decided to get people like him off the streets.

characters.name: Deborah Ciccerone
characters.description: A special FBI agent who goes undercover to befriend Adriana. Aborted Arc: Introduced in the Season 3 finale as an undercover agent who will befriend and gradually groom Adriana to be a federal witness. Her courting process lasts all of two episodes before Christopher tries to fuck her, driving a rift between her and Adriana. At this point, the FBI decides to just arrest their mark and intimidate her into compliance. Deborah is summarily replaced as handler by Robyn Sanservino. Demoted to Extra: Deborah's screentime wanes after she's taken off her mark's case, but she still shows up well into the fifth season. Fair Cop: Part of why she was chosen to go undercover with the mob wives, despite her lack of experience. Also ends up ruining her cover.Harris:You know what the problem was, right? She gave Moltisanti a hard-on.Cubitoso:So, what do we do? Hire only schifosas? False Friend: She goes undercover to befriend Adriana and manipulate information from her, and the latter is deeply hurt when the truth comes out.

characters.name: Frank Grasso
characters.description: A special agent with the FBI and part of the team that searchesDiMeocrime family street boss Tony Soprano's house with a warrant. Category Traitor: Tony is disgusted by the mereconceptof an Italian-American working for the FBI. Of course, as far as Grasso is concerned, Tony is the one betraying the wider Italian-American community by preying on them to enrich himself. Contrived Clumsiness: Tony thinks Grasso purposely breaks a bowl during a register of his house. Hair-Trigger Temper: Easily baited to anger by Tony's insults. Whether this is his true character or an attempt to get Tony's guard down along withContrived Clumsinessis not certain. Shout-Out: His name is an homage to Sonny Grosso, co-author of the bookThe French Connection.

characters.name: Skip Lipari
characters.description: Pussy Bonpensiero's handler. Being Personal Isn't Professional: Rants to Pussy about his frustrations with work. By-the-Book Cop: Although he can be aCowboy Copand evenDirty Copas the job demands, he is professional enough to refuse gifts or bribes from Pussy. Cowboy Cop: The most "mob-like" cop in the show, in both looks and temperament; a mob associate isn't too fazed when Pussy tries to pass him off as "a friend of ours". Although firmly opposed to the mob, he is blunt, abrasive, and confrontational when challenged. Demoted to Extra: He appears in most episodes of Season 2 as an integral part of Pussy’s arc. Afterward, he only appears once, during the FBI bugging operation in the Season 3 premiere.

characters.name: Ron Goddard
characters.description: An FBI agent who is assigned as Harris' new partner when the latter moves over to counter-terrorism. FBI Agent: A new generation one, focused on terrorism and unrelated to the organized crime division. The Stoic: Rather stone-faced and cool. Those Two Guys: Always appears with Harris. What the Hell, Hero?: He doesn't say a word, but his body language screams the trope when Harris reacts to the news ofPhil Leotardo's death with "Damn, we're gonna win this thing!"

characters.name: Leon Wilmore
characters.description: An incorruptible police officer who comes into conflict with Tony. Being Good Sucks: He refuses to accept a bribe from Tony Soprano and writes him a ticket. For this, he loses his overtime pay and is forced to work a degrading retail job at a garden store. Here he once again encounters Tony, who feels remorseful for Wilmore's situation and offers him several hundred dollars unconditionally, which Wilmore refuses yet again. Butt-Monkey: He's punished for holding a wealthy and powerful man accountable for his crimes. What's particularly galling about it is that Tony was clearly in the wrong and the fine was a small amount of money that he was more than capable of covering, meaning Tony had his career sabotaged because his pride was wounded. By-the-Book Cop: This is his personality and archetype. The Fettered: He is shown to be honorable and an upstanding police officer.

characters.name: Vin Makazian
characters.description: A corrupt cop on Tony's payroll. Abusive Parents: His father. Alas, Poor Villain: Yes, he was a slimy, corrupt asshole, but it's hard not to feel bad for him in the leadup to his death, as he's shown to be a pathetic, broken mess whose life comes apart. Cassandra Truth: He outs Big Pussy as an informant to Tony, but Tony later dismisses this due to potentially confusing Pussy for Jimmy Altieri, and finding that Vin owed Pussy a lot of money, so he would have reason to want Pussy dead. Dirty Cop: A corrupt but deeply troubled cop.Even in his tragic last moments, there's some bitter irony in the fact that he still abuses the power of his badge to cut in a traffic queue and get to the edge of the bridge faster.

characters.name: Barry Haydu
characters.description: A veteran New Jersey policeman. Ambiguous Situation: There's no way to tell ifTonyis saying the truth about his past or if it's just part of his scheme to bond with Christopher, his intended successor. Hence, most of his tropes are "according to Tony". WhileThe Many Saints of Newarkshowsit was actually Junior who orchestrated Dickie's death, it remains ambiguous if Haydu was the trigger man as the character's face and name are not revealed to the audience. Dirty Cop: In bed with the mob due to his gambling addiction, he carried out a series of contract killings toWork Off the Debt. The Gambling Addict: Led toTrapped by Gambling Debts. Make It Look Like an Accident: Chris kills him and then plants a gun on the man to make the crime scene look like a suicide. This is not the brightest move, as Chris had fired multiple rounds into Haydu.

characters.name: Dr. Jennifer Melfi
characters.description: An Italian-American psychiatrist and in some ways confidant of Mafia boss Tony Soprano. All Girls Want Bad Boys: It becomes such a problem,Jennifer ends up seeing her own head doctor to deal with her growing attraction to Tony. Finally, she admits to her problem and is able to strongly refuse Tony's advances by the end of the series. All Therapists Are Muggles: A non-supernatural version, where "Muggle" means "somebody not involved withThe Mafia". Tony initially tells her that he's a waste management consultant. That said,she quickly figures outwhat Tony'srealoccupation is. The Artifact: The therapy scenes are a key part of the show in the first season in particular, but the show gradually moves away from them and it becomes clear that if therapy is helping Tony in any way, it is to sharpen his skills as a criminal. Eventually, the Tony-Melfi scenes mostly become a way of recapping the latest goings-on in the plot. What arguably makes this status more clear is that there are multiple examples from season two onwards of Tony quitting therapy for a span of a few episodes and the show doesn't really fall apart as a result. Audience Surrogate: Played with. While she doesn't see the exact details of Tony's life, she's been with him since the beginning of the show and listened to some of his most private confessions. Like most viewers, she's sometimes charmed by him and oftentimes disturbed by his lifestyle and mindset. She also slowly stops humoring his callous behavior and is even one of the few characters tocut him out of her life entirely.

characters.name: Artie Bucco
characters.description: Tony's childhood friend, who now owns a restaurant. Acquired Situational Narcissism: Due to his need to feel important, Artie consistently and smirkingly overestimates his own (non-culinary) abilities and personal charm. This leads him into regularHumiliation Congasthat last for most of the series. Angry Chef: Whilst he projects an affable front, the high levels of stress involved with his job coupled with everything that comes from being a friend of Tony's means he's never too far from snapping. Awful Wedded Life: Are Artie and Charmaine in the same scene? Then they're arguing. They seem to absolutely detest each other. However, they seem to have worked things out by the end of the series and are no longer arguing. Bad Boss: Slightly towards Martina, for spurning his advances.

characters.name: Charmaine Bucco
characters.description: Artie's wife and hostess at the Vesuvius. Divorce Is Temporary: Separates from Artie and asks for a divorce, but it doesn't take and they reconcile. The Dog Bites Back: After getting fed up with Carmela's condescending attitude and treatment of her, Charmaine reveals that she had a fling with Tony in high school and he was going to dump Carmela for her. However, she chose to end things and is content with her choice, leaving Carmela speechless. Fanservice with a Smile: Lowers her neckline and shows more cleavage to attract male clientele. The Glasses Gotta Go: Said by her husband, because the glasses work against the fanservice.

characters.name: Marianucci "Nucci" Gualtieri
characters.description: Paulie Walnuts' mother.It's later revealed she's actually his aunt and adopted him as an infant. Due to the Dead: Dies off-screen on the same episode asChristopher, whose wake overshadows Nucci's. Paulie sees this as a final insult from beyond the grave byChris. Even Bad Men Love Their Mamas: Serves as proof that Paulie isn't totally evil. I Am Not Your Father: Paulie is actually the son of her sister, knocked up by a sailor. Nucci took responsibility for the boy and raised him as her own. When Paulie finds out, he disowns Nucci and has a major identity crisis. Eventually, they reconcile, though. Kindhearted Simpleton: She just isn't very bright, from being tricked into a panic attack by Ralphie's ridiculous lies to annoying other retirees with her slowness. Paulie however couldn't possibly have had a kinder or more forgiving mother figure, which probably explains why he is the way he is.

characters.name: Liz La Cerva
characters.description: Adriana La Cerva's mother. Alcoholic Parent: Carmela and Tony comment on this during "The Ride". Subverted in that Liz claims not to have had a drink in years. She's just depressed followingAdriana's disappearance. Beauty Inversion: She doesn't look any worse than the other mob wives/moms in most of her appearances. By Season 6, she becomes depressed enough to not bother keeping up with the Jersey fashion. Bungled Suicide: After she loses Adriana and everyone around her disregards her theories surrounding the matter, she ends up trying to kill herself. Cassandra Truth: She minces no words when she tells Adriana that Christopher is not a good man and getting engaged to him would be a big mistake that will destroy her life. She turns out to be 100% correct.

characters.name: Father Phil
characters.description: A priest who is close to Carmela. As the Good Book Says...: Frequently dips into Bible verses, but a funny example is when he does an impression ofRobert De Niroas Jesus. Big Eater: He's a massive foodie, often helping himself to the fine Italian cuisine in the Soprano household. Tony refers to him as "MonsignorJughead" when he correctly guesses who ate all the ziti.Carmela speculates that food is somehow involved in his sexual manipulation games with the mob wives, implying that he has a strange fetish for it. Judging by his reaction, she may have been on the money. Carmela speculates that food is somehow involved in his sexual manipulation games with the mob wives, implying that he has a strange fetish for it. Judging by his reaction, she may have been on the money. Demoted to Extra: A major character in the first season, but makes only occasional appearances after it.

characters.name: Robert Wegler
characters.description: AJ's high school guidance counselor who begins an affair with Carmela. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Carmela's final assessment of him, after he feels - not without grounds - that she's using him to help an undeserving A.J. Gentleman and a Scholar: A suave and cultured man, a refreshing change for Carmela. The Ghost: Mentioned a few times in Seasons 4 and 5 before finally appearing in "All Happy Families". Hot Teacher: This is how Carmela sees him.

characters.name: Georgie Santorelli
characters.description: A bartender at the Bada Bing. The Bus Came Back: It turns outthe busnever left. In "Walk Like a Man", he's shown tending the bar as usual on the background while Tony hits on some stripper. Butt-Monkey: He's a walkingpunching bag. Tony tends to beat him up whenever he's frustrated. Tellingly, in one of his few appearances in which he *doesn't* get beaten up by Tony, he gets a severe eye injury from Ralphie instead. Digging Yourself Deeper: He has a habit of doing or saying something stupid and then continuing to do so until someone (usually Tony) has had enough and beats him up. Dumb Muscle: He's a big, burly guy, but he can't seem to figure out how to work a telephone.

characters.name: Elliot Kupferberg
characters.description: Dr. Melfi's therapist. Admiring the Abomination: He's a hardass about sociopathy, but at the same time he is fascinated by Tony Soprano, and not only in a clinical way, as he closely follows the Mafia power play too. Author Avatar: In a roundabout way, perhaps partially unintentional by David Chase. Despite how slimy and smug Elliot is, he is the one to point out Melfi'sCritical Psychoanalysis Failure, so much that he manages to get under her skin. Elliot is the one to let both her and the audience know that they've been enthralled by people who are ultimately irredeemable gangsters. Book Smart: Clearly very intelligent, so intelligent that he points out how Melfi messed up with Tony and how she essentially helped him sharpen his criminal skills. Dr. Jerk: While he sincerely is trying to help Melfi, he's also a smug, judgmental prick who will go as far to humiliate his client if it means getting it in her head to let go of Tony.

characters.name: Blanca Selgado
characters.description: A Puerto Rican woman who briefly dates AJ in Season 6. All Girls Want Bad Boys: Initially what drew her to date A.J. in the first place. Even though she appreciates how he treats her, she slowly realizes he's less of a competent mobster and more of a passive manchild. Dating What Daddy Hates: While Carmela doesn't show it in front of A.J. and Blanca, she's clearly unhappy with the fact her son is dating a dark-skinned Latina who is a good deal older than A.J and already has a child. Tony at least takes comfort in the fact Blanca is a fellow Catholic. Good Parents: Has a young son who she cares about very deeply. Morality Pet: She and her son Hector inspire a major improvement in A.J.'s attitude.

characters.name: Svetlana Kirilenko
characters.description: Cousin of Tony's mistress Irina, and caretaker to Livia. The Caretaker: Livia's nurse. Foil: To Janice. Svetlana is a reliable, down-to-earth, and zero-nonsense character. After a silly dispute, their antagonism reaches a point where Tony has to meddle in professional quality. Also serves as a foil to her cousin Irina, who has a great body but is a childish emotional trainwreck. The Ghost: First mentioned in episode 5, she doesn't appear until the Season 2 finale. Inspirationally Disadvantaged: Having only one leg is not a handicap to her, and Tony admires her for it.Lampshaded, as Svetlana calls Tony out for how patronizing this attitude is.

characters.name: Bruce and Jeannie Cusamano
characters.description: The next-door neighbors of the Sopranos. Damn, It Feels Good to Be a Gangster!: Bruce and his friends are fascinated by the Mafia mythology and are casually curious about it. During a golfing trip, they treat Tony like a zoo animal and pepper him incessantly with Mafia questions. Demoted to Extra: They have a recurring presence throughout the first few seasons of the show, as they're the Sopranos' neighbors and Bruce was the one who recommended Dr. Melfi to Tony in the first place. As the show went on, though, their screentime grew more fleeting, to the point where their only appearances in the latter half of the show come from a drop-in Bruce makes in "Whitecaps" and a blink-and-you-miss-it cameo the two make in "Soprano Home Movies". Doctor's Orders: From time to time, as Bruce is the Sopranos' family physician and the one who referred Tony to Dr. Melfi. Embarrassing Nickname: Tony sometimes calls Dr. Cusamano "Cooze". Heh heh heh.

characters.name: Dr. Ira Fried
characters.description: A well-known urologist who frequently associates with Tony, being a regular player in the Executive Game. Back-Alley Doctor: Averted; he has a well-respected medical practice in New York, but he's still called in to perform emergency surgeries for mob-related injuries. Cunning People Play Poker: He's one of the regular faces at Tony's poker table, skilled enough to hold his own against mobsters and other players. Open Heart Dentistry: While he's a urologist who specializes in erectile dysfunction, he can still perform operations outside of his area, such as patching up Furio after he got shot by Jackie Aprile Jr.

characters.name: Anthony Infante
characters.description: Brother-in-law of John Sacramoni and his spokesperson. The Consigliere: Pretty much the last real ally and advisor Johnny Sack has. He gives his opinion on his brother-in-law's decisions and even gives him the honest truth about how the mob world saw "The King of New York". Establishing Character Moment: One of his first scenes appears to be aVillains Out Shoppingmoment, but it turns out to be a professional meeting in his optical shop. He's a mild civilian who is in over his head among hardened gangsters and is acting out of loyalty to his family. Fish Out of Water: He's the last connection Johnny Sack has to the mob world and has to deal with guys like Tony. He's also a meek guy who runs an eyewear store. Mouth of Sauron: Semi-obligatory. Serves as Johnny Sack's meek spokesperson.

characters.name: Noah Tannenbaum
characters.description: Meadow's college boyfriend. Ambiguous Situation: Was he breaking off his relationship with Meadow entirely his own decision? It is implied that it would very likely have happened anyway at some point, but it is quite possible his father might have forced the issue because he disapproved of his son dating aMafia Princess. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: He initially comes across as an intelligent and decent guy who's a good boyfriend to Meadow despite the family drama. However, as their relationship continues, it's shown that he's more selfish and entitled than he initially lets on. He insists to Meadow that he's aNice Guy, and not like the other college boys, because he's sensitive with her and compassionate towards her roommate. However, it takes a single mediocre essay grade to cause him to rail cruelly against the latter, and once he sleeps with Meadow, his interest in her quickly tanks. The B Grade: He acts as if a single C- on a paper is going to completely ruin his academic life, blaming Meadow’s distracting roommate for it. His father even files arestraining orderagainst her. Black and Nerdy: He's a very intelligent and well-spoken young man as well as half black.

characters.name: Len Tannenbaum
characters.description: Noah's father. Attorney for various celebrities. Disproportionate Retribution: Files a restraining order against Caitlin afterNoah gets a low grade. Education Mama: He has an overbearing career obsession, which causes him to pressure his son Noah into attending Columbia University in New York City, where he watches over him like a hawk. Man of Wealth and Taste: An upper-class attorney of corresponding refinement. Meet the In-Laws: The dinner with Meadow doesn't go well for her and is very uncomfortable. She mistakesDick Wolffor a sports commentator and has to lie about her parents' line of work.

characters.name: Caitlin Rucker
characters.description: Meadow's roommate at Columbia. Aborted Arc: She seems to be heading down a self-destructive path in most of her appearances, but there's never any crisis or resolution to it all. Once Noah breaks up with Meadow, partially due to frustrations over Caitlin, she falls out of focus. When we do see her, she seems to have mellowed out all on her own. Country Mouse: She's from a small town in Oklahoma and is excited to be in a big city like New York until it starts getting to her. Mood-Swinger: Goes through cycles of exuberance and numb depression. Ms. Fanservice: When first seen, she's dancing in front of her dorm room window in just panties and a tank top.

characters.name: Finn De Trolio
characters.description: Meadow's college boyfriend, and later fiance. Armor-Piercing Question: Finn's relationship with Meadow finally deteriorates when he points out that her getting him to revealVito's homosexualityto the family will almost certainly getVitokilled if he ever returns to New Jersey, implicating her in mob business for the first time. Audience Surrogate: His primary role is to show how an average person who had the opportunity to bear witness to the reality of mafia society might react. He's horrified. Break the Cutie: As one of the nicer and more sympathetic characters in the series, he gets intimidated by Vito (sometimes to the point of mild sexual harassment, such as with the arm touching at the hospital) and considers fleeing for his own safety. Cassandra Truth: Downplayed. Though on friendly terms with Tony, he's fully aware of the violent, criminal nature of Tony's associates, and is the only character to so explicitly warn Meadow about them, including all but telling her that Tony's associates aregoing to kill Vito. She completely ignores him.

characters.name: Hunter Scangarelo
characters.description: Meadow's troubled friend from high school. Back for the Finale: After not appearing for averylong time, she makes what is essentially a cameo in the last episode. Childhood Friends: Meadow's best friend at the start of the series. Demoted to Extra: After season 1. Foil: The reason for her reappearance in Season 6. She's a medical student, the noble profession that Carmela and Tony wished for their daughter. While both Meadow and Hunter grew up together and have similar backgrounds, Hunter is implied to have experienced much hardship, actually suffering from her misdeeds, and ultimately changing for the better, whereas Meadow, who lived a more sheltered and non-punitive life with doors opened for her, is gearing up to effectively become a mob lawyer.

characters.name: Davey Scatino
characters.description: An old friend of Tony and Artie's from high school who now runs a sporting goods store. And Starring: "AndRobert Patrickas David Scatino" Asshole Victim: Tony actually tries to make him back off from gambling in his games, but Davey forces his way in and promptly runs up even more debt than Tony would have allowed. Davey engenders no sympathy by taking away his son's car to pay off his debts and then blaming his brother-in-law for not helping him after he's lost everything. Beard of Sorrow: When Tony runs into him at the high school graduation, Davey has a day or two of stubble. This shows that he's not doing well, in spite of his claims to the contrary. Butt-Monkey: Davey's life goes downhill in the most exaggerated way possible after he lets his gambling addiction get out of control.

characters.name: Eric Scatino
characters.description: The son of Davey Scatino and a classmate and friend of Meadow's Aesop Collateral Damage: The misfortune he suffers as a result of his dad's gambling shows the audience just how innocent people with no involvement in the mafia whatsoever can be negatively affected by Tony's criminal actions. I Coulda Been a Contender!: He's a bright, straight edge student on his way to attending Georgetown University until his dad loses his college fund to Tony. Unable to afford the expensive tuition, he's forced to attend the considerably less prestigious Montclair State University, where he's so miserable that he turns to drugs as a way to cope. We Used to Be Friends: After he loses his car and college fund to his dad's gambling debts, Eric cuts off his friendship with Meadow as he blames Tony.

characters.name: J.T. Dolan
characters.description: A TV writer who meets Chris Moltisanti in Narcotics Anonymous. Acting Out a Daydream: Anticipating a TV contract in aDick Wolfseries, he brushes off his gambling losses as "a month's salary". The contract never comes to pass... Addiction Displacement: He trades his drug and alcohol addictions for gambling, which only makes things worse for himself in the long run. Boom, Headshot!:How he goes out, courtesy of Chris. Butt-Monkey: Pretty much every appearance has something awful happen to him, usually due to Chris.Chris eventually kills him out of sheer spite when JT tries to cut Chris out of his life for good.

characters.name: Minn Matrone
characters.description: A grumpy old woman living in the same nursing home as Nucci Gualtieri. Alpha Bitch: The nursing home director describes the place as a "high school with wheelchairs". Asshole Victim: Her bullying treatment of Nucci is unlikely to endear her to the audience. As horrific as her death is, it's unlikely many will miss her now that she's gone. Do Not Taunt Cthulhu: She's smart enough to see Paulie for what he is. Unfortunately, she's not smart enough to keep this to herself. Dies Wide Open: Her glassy eyes in death are downright creepy and almost supernatural looking.

characters.name: Carter Chong
characters.description: A patient at a mental hospital who befriends Junior Soprano. Berserk Button: Pretty much anything to do with his father makes him blow his lid. The Dragon: Becomes an odd variant to Junior, helping him to set up illicit card games among the patients. Hair-Trigger Temper: Swings between calm and content to enraged and screaming at a dime. My Beloved Smother: Implied when his mother visits him.

characters.name: Dr. Krakower
characters.description: A psychiatrist and teacher of Dr. Melfi who delivers an ultimatum to Carmela. Brutal Honesty: Whereas Melfi and Elliot play the long game, encouraging their patients to work things out for themselves so they can choose to grow in a positive manner, Krakower comes out swinging and doesn't sugarcoat his words or spare Carmela's feelings at all when laying out the facts to her. Considering her situation and how both of them end up falling for the allure of the criminal life the Sopranos lead, his approach comes off as better for himself at least. Dr. Jerk: A more heroic one than normal, but he's not interested in any kind of gentle approach to helping Carmela grow enough to leave Tony, merely spelling out the facts to her in the bluntest manner possible and making no effort to hide his judgment of her if she doesn't leave him. He also makes clear that he has contempt for modern therapy's more empathic approach, seeing it as enabling and excusing patients' bad behavior rather than working to fix them as he sees as his goal. The show doesn't portray his views as wholly correct, but considering the main therapeutic relationship of the series, it's hard not to see where he's coming from. Good Is Not Nice: He's morally in the right but his prickly demeanor, blunt manner and somewhat less than progressive views of therapy and modern society as a whole (then again, in the context of our main cast...) don't exactly make him the most charismatic character. Jerkass Has a Point: He's far from the nicest guy in the world but his frank assessment of Tony, Carmela's culpability in his behavior, and the fact that she can't change him, as much as she might wish to, and that she can't say she wasn't aware of what being with him would lead to are all dead on.

characters.name: Jim "Johnny Cakes" Witowski
characters.description: ANew Englandbarman and volunteer firefighter who begins an affair with Vito Spatafore. The Ace: A local hero who owns a diner and lives a perfectly balanced life. Did Not Get the Girl: Vito eventually gets bored of his safe civilian life and abandons Jim in the middle of the night. He calls back from New Jersey to apologize, only to be rebuffed by Jim and told in no uncertain terms to never call back again. Firemen Are Hot: A fireman with a ripped body. Last Het Romance: He has a daughter, but it's unclear if his previous relationship was an example of this and Jim came out late in life, or he's just bisexual.

characters.name: Robert "Bobby Jr." III and Sophia Baccalieri
characters.description: The children of Bobby and Karen. Butt-Monkey: Bobby is bullied by AJ and this makes him wary of family meetings. Additionally, both their parents and their paternal grandfather are killed in unpleasant circumstances within the space of a few years, and they have none other than Janice as their stepmother. One-Steve Limit: Bobby is Robert Baccalieri III, but he is simply called Bobby Jr. Trauma Conga Line: Their mother dies and Janice becomes their stepmother. It only gets worse withthe death of their father.

characters.name: Sal Vitro
characters.description: A gardener who gets in the middle of a feud between Paulie and Feech. Butt-Monkey: The poor guy becomes the official gardener for the mob. Even worse when he ends up getting tackled and arrested by the FBI when they raid Johnny Sack's residence. Family Business: His son has to drop out of college to lend a hand because of the ensuing money shortages. No Social Skills: He isn't exactly the most charismatic person. Tony seems annoyed just about whenever he is in his presence and Carmela outright states that he is a 'drip'. Throw the Dog a Bone: His slave-like workload gets happily reduced when Johnny Sack has to change his residence.

characters.name: Bryan Spatafore
characters.description: Brother of Vito and a construction worker. Butt-Monkey: Ends up in a coma because he just happened to be in the wrong place at the wrong time. Golf Clubbing: Mustang Sally beats him badly with a golf club. Innocent Bystander: Gets involved in a street incident when the girlfriend of Mustang Sally turns to him for help. Mugging the Monster: The monster's brother. Mustang Sally pays with his life for the beating of a made man's brother.

characters.name: Alan Sapinsly
characters.description: Attorney and owner of the Whitecaps property. Amoral Attorney: Refuses to return Tony's deposit despite cutting out the previous buyers without a second thought. Jerkass Has a Point: When he hears about Tony's separation from Carmela, he advises Tony to talk to the best divorce lawyers before his wife to establish conflict of interest. This ends up being one of the biggest factors to their marriage mending. Rich in Dollars, Poor in Sense: He's used to intimidating people with legal action. Tony however brushes off all of his threats with ease. Significant Monogram: Has the same initials as Tony. He even has the same photo of Rocky Marciano as the one in the Bing.

characters.name: Ben Kingsley
characters.description: Notable Hollywood actor who Chris and Little Carmine try to cast for Cleaver. As Himself: One of the few celebrities who plays themselves in the Sopranos universe. Blatant Lies: He tries to be diplomatic about it, which is smart considering he's dealing with mobsters, one of whom has killed multiple people, but he can't fully hide his lack of interest in Chris and Carmine or his desire to be far away from them. Precision F-Strike: Let's out one to his assistant when he notices he'll be sharing the same flight as Chris. Surrounded by Idiots: Justifiable in that humoring Chris and Little Carmine is the last thing he'd enjoy doing.

characters.name: Coach Hauser
characters.description: Meadow's soccer coach. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: A pervert posing as a hard-working coach and family man. Creepy Gym Coach: Meadow reveals that he's been sexually abusing Ally Vandermeed, another player on her team. It's enough for even the mob to want to whack him. More Hateable Minor Villain: Most of the antagonists in the series either have some degree of moral complexity (family,lines they wouldn't cross,honor). Hauser is little more than a child molester, to the point that he almost makes characters likeRichieandLivialook good by comparison. Pedophilia Is a Special Kind of Evil: Having an affair with one of his own students who is only a teenager.

characters.name: Coach Molinaro
characters.description: Tony's high school football coach. Disappointed in You: He had high hopes for Tony and was disappointed when he fell into a life of crime. Dream People: He only appears in a dream Tony has, but it's safe to say the real man wasn't too different from the version conjured up by Tony's subconscious. A Father to His Men: He went out of his way to spend extra time with Tony to further his football ambitions and keep him out of trouble. Suffice to say, he's disappointed in how he turned out after high school. Good Is Not Nice: An honest high school football coach who was nonetheless a harsh taskmaster as well as foul mouthed.

characters.name: Hernan O'Brien
characters.description: A.J.'s friend from high school. Slimeball: One of A.J.'s worst friends. He hangs out with A.J. mostly just to use his mob father's clout and makes advances towards underage girls. Toxic Friend Influence: Tony and Carmela do not approve of him. Even Rhiannon admits how bad he was.

characters.name: Rhiannon Flammer
characters.description: A.J.'s friend and eventual girlfriend. Age-Gap Romance: Ends up dating A.J. even though he's 21 and she's a junior in high school. Bourgeois Bohemian: Comes from a family rich enough to keep her in the same rehab as A.J.. She also enjoys David Sedaris and Bob Dylan. Hair of Gold, Heart of Gold: Generally a nice girl who helps bring A.J. out of his depression.

characters.name: Matt Testa
characters.description: A friend of A.J. who regularly hangs out with him. Alcohol-Induced Idiocy: During the stay at Hudson Suites, he ends up getting wasted and doing stupid things, along with everyone else there. Toxic Friend Influence: Often shows up when A.J. is engaging in various substances.

characters.name: Vito Spatafore Jr.
characters.description: Did You Just Flip Off Cthulhu?: He did this to Phil Leotardo, his uncle via his mother (and unbeknownst to him,the murderer of his father), as well as Tony Soprano himself, both infamous mob bosses. Goths Have It Hard: He dresses up as a goth in his final appearance as a rebellion against his school for bullying him, and he ends up being kidnapped and sent to a boot camp. Jerkass Has a Point: He rightly points out that neither Phil or Tony actually give a shit about him or his family and they're only intervening out of a sense of obligation. Teens Are Monsters:Subverted.Vitodoestake a new level in jerkass between Season 6A and 6B, but it is only because he's lashing out against the terrible hand his family was dealt with all of a sudden as well as the bullying at the hands of other thoughtless teens. Trauma Conga Line:Oh dear.First of all, his father Vito has to flee New Jersey after he was outed as gay, then after he comes back,he and his sister are lied tothat he was a CIA agent only to learn the truth once Vito is murdered and the paper insensitively published about his sexuality. He then getsbullied by his peers throughout the next year, leading him to act out as revenge for the bullying. His mother then tells on him to both Phil and Tony, two mob bosses who got his father killed.And as things begin to look up for him due to Marie's suggestion for the family to move to Maine to start anew, Tony thoughtlessly gambles the money which was supposed to go to them and instead cheaps out to send Vito to a boot camp in Idaho where corporal punishment is allowed. His last appearance is him screaming for his mother to save him as he gets essentially kidnapped by the officials as both his mother and sister cry for him but do nothing. It will be a downrightmiracleif he manages to return from the boot camp sane.

characters.name: Richard Aprile Jr.
characters.description: The son of Richie Aprile. Ambiguously Gay: It isn't made clear whether or not he is actually gay or whether Richie is just being prejudiced when he assumes that his son's interest in ballroom dancing means that he is gay. Disproportionate Retribution: On the receiving end. He is apparently disowned by his father completely for the crime of...being good at dancing, which Richie sr. thinks is gay. Even more ridiculous, we have zero evidence other than Richie's word that "Little Ricky"isgay, his father just considers the mere possibility completely unacceptable. One-Shot Character: He only shows up in one episode and doesn't even appear for the funerals of either his uncle Jackie Sr. or his cousin Jackie Jr. Small Role, Big Impact: Despite only appearing in one episode, he becomes the subject of an argument between his father Richie and Janice that ends inJanice shooting Richie dead.

characters.name: Jason and Justin Blundetto
characters.description: The young twin sons of Tony Blundetto. Single-Minded Twins: They basically act as one and always appear together in their scenes. Small Role, Big Impact: They only appear in a few episodes (and all of them in season five), but the jealousy they express towards A.J.'s greater material privilege is what tips their father into accepting the job ofwhacking Joey Peeps, putting him firmly back into 'the game' and leading to a whole lot of other consequences. Trickster Twins: Their antics include messing up the Sopranos' backyard furniture after Carmela allows them to use the pool.

characters.name: Jeremy Herrera
characters.description: A teenager who has a brief fling with Meadow. Hormone-Addled Teenager: This is pretty much his main characteristic. He is interested in making out (and perhaps more) with Meadow even as she is more interested in watching TV. He seems particularly pissed-off when Livia arrives to interrupt them. Mixed Ancestry Is Attractive: He is Dominican and is one of two boyfriends (the other being Noah) of Meadow's to be of a mixed-race background. One-Shot Character: Has a grand total of one scene. Not referred to prior to it or since, despite there being potential conflict with Meadow's parents due to his Dominican heritage. Temporary Love Interest: It isn't known how long he and Meadow had been involved with or interested in each other prior to their on-screen making out, but his purpose in terms of the plot seems to solely be to show how Meadow is exploring her sexuality as a highschooler.

characters.name: Teddy Spirodakis
characters.description: A Greek-American gambler from Boston, Massachusetts. All for Nothing: Eugene kills Teddy as a favor to Chris to earn him some goodwill with upper management, hoping that Tony will approve his plans to semi-retire and move to Florida. Tony still rejects Eugene's Florida plan, as do the feds who he is secretly snitching to, so Eugene ends up hanging himself not long after killing Teddy. Boom, Headshot!: Gets three, courtesy of Eugene Pontecorvo. Call-Forward:He's fat, has the initials TS, and is murdered in a restaurant by a man wearing a Members Only jacket in the first episode of season 6. In the last episode of Season 6 (and the series), Tony Soprano's death is implied to have come in the exact same manner as Teddy's, even down to the Members Only jacket-wearing hitman. Fat Slob: He's a heavy man who is seen messily eating in a fast food restaurant in his only appearance.

characters.name: "Man In Members Only Jacket"
characters.description: A man who enters the Holsten's diner in the final scene. He sits at the counter, glances twice at the Sopranos's table, then stands up, walking past the table before entering the restroom. Ambiguous Situation: He could be just another patron with an elevated amount of screentime to amp up the feelings of paranoia, ora hitman. Call-Back: In the first episode of Season 6, Eugene Pontecorvo kills a heavyset man with the initials TS in a restaurant while wearing a Members Only jacket. In the final episode of Season 6 (and the series),this is strongly implied to be what possibly happens to Tony Soprano at the hands of this character. No Name Given: Just credited as "Man in Members Only Jacket". Face of a Thug: The man certainly looks "mobbed up", and he wears the same kind of jacket wore by Eugene Pontecorvo during a killing in the Season 6 premiere.

characters.name: Tony Soprano
characters.description: Abusive Parents:In flashbacks, both of his parents are portrayed as highly manipulative and callousnarcissistswho regularly prioritized their own needs at their children's expense. Whereas Tony's father is portrayed as a corrupting influence who was alarmingly indifferent to his children's emotional well-being, his mother, Livia, is revealed to have regularly subjected Tony and his siblings to physical and emotional abuse that has left them psychologically scarred as adults.Zig-Zaggedregarding his behavior towards A.J. and Meadow, particularly starting from the third season. While he genuinely loves and ultimately cares for their well-beings, he's emotionally and verbally abusive towards both of them (more-so the former) fairly often, has threatened physical violence towards them at least once, has little issue intimidating them if he feels the need to, and generally does little to shield them fromhis temper tantrums, among other things. He's definitely a better parent to A.J. and Meadow than his own parents were towards him, but he's stillveryflawed.
